SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S. 1, Special Branch Station 52/3
REPORT
Date January 30, 1940.
Subject (in full) Letter from Chief of Water Police Main Corps to Messrs.
Jardine Matheson's Ships' compradores.
Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to previous reports regarding letters
sent by Pau Ts Ying (鮑子英), the Chief of the Water
Police Main Corps, Pootung, to Compradores operating on
ships of the Indo China Steam Navigation Company,
attached hereto are copies of replies written by Liang
Ching (陳良清), comprador of the s.s. "TAKSANG"
and Wu Bak Sung (胡柏生), comprador of the s.s.
"WINGSANG", to Pau Ts Ying.

At the time that the compradores received the
letters from the Water Police Headquarters, it was
suggested by this office that the compradores advise
Pau Ts Ying, by letter, that they themselves were not
responsible for the dismissal of members of the crew.
This advice has been followed by the compradores
concerned and copies of their replies forwarded to
this office for information.

Killingbeck
D. P. S.
A. C. (Special Branch).

日期：1940年1月30日。
主题（全称）：水警总队队长致怡和洋行轮船买办的信函。
由 D.P.S. Killingbeck 撰写，由 D. I. Crawford 转呈。

关于此前报告的浦东水警总队队长鲍子英（Pau Ts Ying）致印度支那轮船公司（Indo China Steam Navigation Company）所属轮船买办的信件，现附上“泰山”轮（s.s. "TAKSANG"）买办陈良清（Liang Ching）和“永昌”轮（s.s. "WINGSANG"）买办胡柏生（Wu Bak Sung）回复鲍子英的信件副本。

当买办们收到水警总局的信件时，本处建议买办们通过书信告知鲍子英，他们本人对船员被解雇一事不负责任。相关买办已采纳此建议，并将其回复副本送交本处备案。

Killingbeck
D. P. S.
助理总监（特务科）。

（印：KWING SANG）

January 15, 1940.

Captain Ts Ying,

Your letter has been received. The cabin
boys named Zee Ah Yoong, Sung Ah Nyi and Oo Ah
Mau were dismissed some time ago by the Captain,
upon instructions from the management, who were
dissatisfied with their services. I had nothing
to do with this matter. Moreover, staff-affairs
and other affairs are all in the hands of the
captain while I remain impartial towards cabin
boys and tallymen. I have heard nothing relating
to the cause of the dismissal of the cabin boys
and you had better make enquiries at the Company.

I regret very much being unable to visit
you owing to press me of work and the immediate
departure of the ship, but hope that you will
excuse me.

Yours sincerely,
WOO PAH SUNG.
Chopped: S.S. "Wing Sang"
Compradore Office.
page_data.zh:
1940年1月15日。

子英船长，

来信收悉。名为 Zee Ah Yoong、Sung Ah Nyi 和 Oo Ah Mau 的茶房侍者已于前些时候由船长根据公司管理层的指示予以解雇，管理层对他们的服务感到不满。此事与我无关。此外，人事及其他事务均由船长掌管，而我对茶房侍者和理货员保持中立。我未听闻有关解雇这些茶房侍者的原因，你最好向公司查询。

因工作繁忙且船只即将离港，我很遗憾无法拜访你，望见谅。

此致，
胡柏生（WOO PAH SUNG）。

page_data.en:
Translation of a despatch, dated January 23, 1940,
addressed to Pau Ts Ying (子英), the Chief of
the Water Police Main Corps, Footung, by Lung Liang
Ching (陳良清), Comprador of the s.s. "Taksing" of
the Jardine Matheson & Company.

With reference to the dismissal of Pei Hung Zien
(畢鴻生) and Tung Ah Foo (董阿福), seamen of the s.s.
"TAKSING", I beg to inform you that I was not instrumental
in effecting their discharge. The reason for their dismissal
was that, due to the undesirable attitude adopted by these
two seamen towards the superior officers, the Captain of
the s.s. "TAKSING" submitted a report to the company
authority which consequently effected their dismissal.
It must be pointed out that it is stipulated by the regulations
of the company that only the company authority has the
right to employ or discharge the employees and that only
those who are in possession of certificates issued by
the company and signed by the British Consulate General
are allowed to obtain positions on the vessels.

It is entirely incorrect that I discharged these
two seamen for private reasons. Enquiries made directly
to the company authority will elicit the truth.
page_data.zh:
怡和洋行“泰兴”轮（s.s. "Taksing"）买办陈良清（Lung Liang Ching）于1940年1月23日致浦东水警总队队长鲍子英（Pau Ts Ying）的信函译文。

关于“泰兴”轮（s.s. "TAKSING"）海员毕鸿生（Pei Hung Zien）和董阿福（Tung Ah Foo）被解雇一事，谨告知阁下，我并未参与促成他们的解雇。解雇原因是这两名海员对上级官员态度恶劣，“泰兴”轮船长向公司当局提交报告，从而导致他们被解雇。必须指出，根据公司规章规定，只有公司当局有权雇用或解雇员工，且只有持有由公司签发并经英国总领事馆签署证书的人员，方获准在船上任职。

称我因私人原因解雇这两名海员完全是不实的。直接向公司当局查询即可得知真相。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section I, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 293 A
Date: April 25th, 40.

Subject Chung Kuo Seamen's General Labour Union - Pamphlets
distributed.

Made by. D.P.S. Killingbeck. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

（批：See also D. 8453）

Attached hereto is a notice which has
recently been sent to the tallymen on the s.s.
"Taksang" and the tea-boys of the s.s. "Yu Sang",
both of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company,
by the so-called Chung Kuo Seamen's General
Labour Union. They have no doubt been distributed
in an effort to persuade the men to join the Union,
but it is not very likely that they will have any
effect, as the fact that the management of the
Company do not acknowledge any of the Labour Unions
is well known to the crews of the vessels.

Efforts have been made in the past by the
Chung Hwa Seamen's Union to obtain the re-instatement
of several tea-boys dismissed by the Company, but
proceedings locally were discontinued after letters
had been written by the ships' compradores to the
Water Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government,
stating that the compradores themselves were not
responsible for the dismissals.

Apparently the union officials have since
been negotiating with the Japanese Gendarmerie at
Tangku in order to cause the arrest of the comprador
of the s.s. "Taksang". A copy of a letter written
by Mr. N.A. BOURNES, of the Indo-China Steam Navigation
Company, to the Shipping Manager of the Company,
concerning the affair at Tientsin, is attached for
information.

D.C.(Special Branch ).

Killingbeck
D. P. S.

报告
档案号 293 A
日期：1940年4月25日。

主题：中国海员总工会 - 分发传单。

由 D.P.S. Killingbeck 撰写。由 D. I. Crawford 转呈。

（批注：另见 D. 8453）

现附上所谓“中国海员总工会”近期发送给印度支那轮船公司所属“泰兴”轮（s.s. "Taksang"）理货员和“裕昌”轮（s.s. "Yu Sang"）茶房的通告。这些传单无疑是为了劝说工人加入工会而分发的，但不太可能产生任何效果，因为各船船员均知悉公司管理层不承认任何工会这一事实。

过去，中华海员公会曾努力争取让被公司解雇的几名茶房复职，但在轮船买办致函上海市政府水警局声明买办本人对解雇事宜不负责任后，本地的诉讼程序即告中止。

显然，工会官员此后一直在与塘沽的日本宪兵队谈判，企图导致“泰兴”轮买办被捕。现附上印度支那轮船公司 N.A. BOURNES 先生致公司航运经理关于天津事件的信函副本，以供参考。

副总监（特务科）。

Killingbeck
D. P. S.

page_data.en:
Translation of a Notice issued by the Chung Kuo
Seamen's General Labour Union and addressed to the
Staff of the s.s. "Taksang" during March 1940.

Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in August 1937 and the subsequent general retreat of the Chinese
troops from Shanghai, the former Chung Hwa Seamen's General
Labour Union accordingly removed to Hankow and then to Chungking.
Therefore, should the members employed on board ships in the lower
course of the Yangtsze River experience any trouble, the union
could not mediate because of its absence from these parts, thus
leaving the members unprotected for the past two years.

Last Spring, our Chairman Wang Cailing Wei, dissatisfied
with the conspiracy between the Chungking Government and the
Communists, left Chungking and started to promote the Anti-Comintern,
Peace and National Reconstruction Campaign which gains the support
of the people of the country and the 800,000 members of our union.
Even the ex-employees of the now defunct Chung Hwa Seamen's General
Labour Union arrived in Shanghai and participated in the peace
movements.

On October 24, 1939, by order of the Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Kuomintang headquarters, the name of the former
Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union was changed into the
present name Chung Kuo Seamen's General Labour Union, and one Wang
Pan Wei and 13 others were nominated Committee members of the new
Union. The Committee members on the following day held an
inaugural meeting and began to function with offices at 7b Jess-
field Road. Furthermore, on October 28, 1939 one Zung Yuen
Loong and 9 others were appointed to prepare the formation of a
page_data.zh:
中国海员总工会于1940年3月期间发布并致“泰兴”轮（s.s. "Taksang"）全体职员的通告译文。

继1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发及随后中国军队从上海全面撤退后，原中华海员总工会随之迁往汉口，继而迁往重庆。因此，若受雇于长江下游船舶的会员遭遇任何困难，工会因不在该地区而无法进行调解，致使会员在过去两年中处于无保护状态。

去年春季，我方主席汪精卫（Wang Cailing Wei，音译，注：此处原文拼写疑似指汪精卫 Wang Jingwei，但按指令保留原文拼音并音译）因不满重庆政府与共产党之间的阴谋，离开重庆，开始推动反共产国际、和平与建国运动，该运动获得了全国民众及我方80万会员的支持。甚至已解散的原中华海员总工会的前雇员也抵达上海，参与了和平运动。

1939年10月24日，奉国民党总部社会部命令，原中华海员总工会更名为现在的中国海员总工会，并提名王攀伟（Wang Pan Wei，音译）等13人为新工会委员。委员们于次日举行就职会议，并在杰斯菲尔德路7b号（Jessfield Road 7b，即今万航渡路）设立办事处开始运作。此外，1939年10月28日，任命宗元龙（Zung Yuen Loong，音译）等9人筹备成立

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Shanghai Branch Office, while one Ting Tse Hwang and 9 others
were to do the same in Hankow.

The former Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union,
situated in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North Honan
Road, was ordered to disorganize on February 24, 1940 and to
amalgamate with the present union which is now busily engaged in
handling the registration of seamen and marine matters. Efforts
are also being made to revive the branch offices at various ports.
Registration for both old and new members is at present
in force.

Standing Committee :- Lee Kai-zung 李凱縱
                     Dang Yan-wei 鄧彥威
                     Loo Kwang-lai 羅廣來

1.5. Address of the Shanghai Branch Office is at the 3rd floor
of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Honan Road.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

上海分会，同时任命丁泽黄（Ting Tse Hwang，音译）等9人在汉口进行同样的筹备工作。

位于河南北路中国商会大楼内的原中华海员总工会，奉命于1940年2月24日解散，并与目前正忙于处理海员登记及海事事务的现工会合并。各方也在努力恢复各港口的分会。目前正在进行新老会员的登记工作。

常务委员会：李凯纵（Lee Kai-zung）
                     邓彦威（Dang Yan-wei）
                     罗广来（Loo Kwang-lai）

1.5. 上海分会地址位于河南北路中国商会三楼。

I.C. NO. 199
JARDINE, MATHESON & CO., LTD.
(INCORPORATED IN HONGKONG)

Coy    apl 22nd 1940

SONGMIKE
by Songmike
Shipping & cargo.

Dear Sir,

Re Union Trouble at Tientsin.

On Saturday the 20th inst. I met by chance
ex Compradore of S/S Dahpu and brother of our
Chief Compradore on S/S Yak Sang.
He has been at Tientsin for the past
month & on the 10th inst. he was informed by the
2nd Compradore of S/S Yak Sang that the Union
officials were negotiating with the Japanese
Gendarmerie with intent to cause the arrest of
the Yak Sang Compradore & requested that he
mediate in the matter.
Together with a Chinese friend who
could speak Japanese he called on the Japanese
Gendarmerie Commander at Tientsin & requested his
assistance. He was advised to go to Tang Ku
& interview the local Japanese Gendarmes.
This he did & on the 11th inst. he
invited the Commandant together with the Japanese
Chief of Tang Ku Water Police & two others, to
dinner on board the Yak Sang.

公司    1940年4月22日

宋迈克（SONGMIKE）
由 Songmike 代笔
航运及货物部。

尊敬的先生：

关于天津的工会纠纷。

本月20日（星期六），我偶然遇见了“大浦”轮（S/S Dahpu）的前买办，他也是我们在“雅昌”轮（S/S Yak Sang）上的首席买办的兄弟。
他在天津待了一个月，本月10日，“雅昌”轮的二买办通知他，工会官员正在与日本宪兵队谈判，意图逮捕“雅昌”轮买办，并请他从中调解。
他与一位懂日语的中国朋友一起拜访了天津的日本宪兵队司令，请求其协助。对方建议他去塘沽会见当地的日本宪兵。
他照办了，并于本月11日邀请司令官以及塘沽水警的日本主管和其他两人，在“雅昌”轮上共进晚餐。

page_data.en:
I.C. NO. 189
JARDINE, MATHESON & CO., LTD.
(INCORPORATED IN HONGKONG)

During dinner the Union Trouble was discussed
& the Japanese left saying that they would not
render any assistance to the Union
Asked whether he had paid any money
to the Japanese or to any other person to settle the
matter he replied in the negative; but that the
dinner drinks and his trip to Tientsin had
cost him between $300 & $400.=
Asked whether he thought that the
Union would continue to make trouble he replied
that they were sure to do so, but that without
Japanese backing they were harmless.

(The above mentioned trouble was over the
2 dismissed stelops whom the Union are
trying to get reinstated on our ship)

内部通信编号 189
怡和洋行有限公司
（在香港注册）

晚宴期间讨论了工会纠纷，日本人离开时表示不会向工会提供任何协助。
当被问及是否向日本人或其他任何人支付款项以解决此事时，他予以否认；但表示晚宴酒水及他的天津之行花费了他300至400美元。
当被问及他认为工会是否会继续制造麻烦时，他回答说他们肯定会这样做，但在没有日本支持的情况下，他们是无害的。

（上述提到的纠纷是关于两名被解雇的司炉工，工会正试图让他们在我们的船上复职）

Subject (in full) Jardine Matheson Company: Bonus granted to Chinese Employees.
Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by C. Crawford J. 8
With reference to attached report, which
appeared in the "China Press" dated August 31,
concerning special subsidies granted to Chinese
employees of the Jardine Matheson Company, en-
quiries reveal that a special allowance has been
granted to the employees in view of the high cost
of living prevailing in Shanghai.
The allowances came into effect approximate-
ly two weeks ago and were granted voluntarily by
the management of the Company, without any applica-
tion having been received from the workers.

由 D.P.S. Killingbeck 撰写，由 C. Crawford J. 8 转呈。
关于附件中刊登于8月31日《字林西报》（China Press）上有关怡和洋行授予华籍雇员特别津贴的报告，经查询证实，鉴于上海生活成本高昂，公司已向雇员发放特别津贴。

CHINA PRESS

AUG 31 1939

135,000 Workers To
Get Subsidy From
Big Local Company

In view of the increased cost of
living in Shanghai resulting from
the devaluation of the Chinese
dollar in the local black market,
the management of the Jardine
Matheson Company has decided to
give special subsidies to its 135,000
Chinese staff members and workers,
according to the Ta Mei Wan Pao,
released by China News and Views
Digest.
Those who receive a salary of
more than $100 will receive a
subsidy of twenty per cent as from
August 1, 1939 and those receive
less than $100 will receive a sub-
sidy of twenty-five per cent. As a
result, the company will pay
$1,000,000 more every month
as salaries and wages to the Chin-
ese staff members and workers.

L.B.S. Ellinghaus
C. 31/8
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年8月31日

本地大公司将为
13.5万名工人
提供补贴

据《大美晚报》（Ta Mei Wan Pao）报道（由《中国新闻观察文摘》发布），鉴于当地黑市上中国货币贬值导致上海生活成本增加，怡和洋行管理层决定向其13.5万名华籍职员和工人提供特别补贴。
月薪超过100元者，自1939年8月1日起将获得20%的补贴；月薪低于100元者将获得25%的补贴。因此，公司每月将额外支付100万美元作为华籍职员和工人的薪金及工资。

L.B.S. Ellinghaus
C. 1939年8月31日

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Crawford D.D

Enquiries show that Dzien Hung-quin, age about 40,
a native of Chekiang Province, at present resides in an
upstaires front room of the Kung Woo Ziang Native Tobacco
Shop (公和祥皮絲烟店), Poo An Li Alleyway, Rue
Montauban (the rear part of the premises being No. 206
Boulevard des deux Republiques), was employed on the s.s.
Woosung of the China Navigation Company (Butterfield &
Swire) until about one year ago and participated in the
activities of the former Chung Hwa Seamen's Union. Recently,
Chen Yuen Loong, ex-Chairman of the defunct "Two Steamship
Tallymen's Club" residing at No. 5 Boo Fah Fong (蒲柏坊),
Avenue Dubail, has endeavoured to secure the assistance of
Dzien Hung-quin with a view to the establishment of an
employment bureau known as the "Introduction Agency for
Unemployed Seamen", which is still in the preparatory stage.
Chen Yuen Loong is said to have informed Dzien Hung-quin
that his present abode would be utilized as an office for

Subject Chen Yuen Loong (陳元龍) - Renewal of Activities

Made by/ and Forwarded by U.D.I. Ross

Chen Yuen Loong, ex-chairman of the defunct
"Two Steamship Tallymen's Club" who resides at No.5
200 Pah Wong (蒲柏坊), Avenue Dubail, was interviewed
at headquarters on January 24 and gave the following
information :

Following the withdrawal of Chinese troops from
Shanghai in November, 1937, he accompanied General Yang
Hu, former Defence Commissioner of Woosung and Shanghai
and concurrently Special Delegate for Seamen's Affairs,
to Hankow and remained there until September, 1938, when
he returned to Shanghai. Upon arrival he learned of the
unemployment of a number of tallymen of Messrs. Jardine
Matheson & Co. through trade depression. In view of
his many acquaintances among the compradores of ships of
various steamship companies, he decided to establish a
Tallymen's Employment Agency at the above address, his
object being to find work for those unemployed tallymen
through the medium of the compradores of ships. So far
he has obtained employment for over sixty tallymen with
compradores of Jardines while forty others are still on
the waiting list. He states that he does not collect
any registration or introduction fee but admits that he
receives 50 cents per mensem from each person, for whom
he has secured employment, as long as he is employed with
the company.

On or about December 8, 1938, Chen met Mr.N. Bourne,
Chief of Smuggling Prevention Section of Jardines at the

陈元龙，已解散的“轮船理货员俱乐部”前主席，居住于爱多亚路蒲柏坊 (Pah Wong) 5号200室，于1月24日在总部接受问询，并提供如下信息：

继1937年11月中国军队撤离上海后，他陪同前吴淞及上海防务专员兼海员事务特派员杨虎将军前往汉口，并留居该地直至1938年9月返回上海。抵沪后，他获悉因贸易萧条导致怡和洋行 (Jardine Matheson & Co.) 多名理货员失业。鉴于他在各轮船公司买办中熟识众多，他决定在上述地址设立一家理货员职业介绍所，旨在通过轮船买办的中介为那些失业的理货员寻找工作。迄今为止，他已通过怡和洋行的买办为六十多名理货员谋得职位，另有四十人仍在候补名单上。他声称不收取任何登记费或介绍费，但承认从他为其谋得职位的每个人那里，只要其受雇于该公司，每月收取50分。

Information has been received to the effect that
Chen Yuen-loong (陳元龍) ex-chairman of the "Tallymen's
Club" and former staff member of the Chung Hwa Seamen's Union
has renewed his activities on the Shanghai waterfront,
setting up an employment agency at the Roosevelt Terminal,

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Trouble between 2nd Steward and Cabin-Boys on S.S. "Loongwo"
Sir,
With reference to the remarks of the P.A. to D.C. (Crime) on Diary 1, page 3, of this case re charging the four cabin-boys with Intimidation, the reason why the case was not treated as an ordinary case of Intimidation and immediate action taken was because the vessel had already sailed when the report was received and moreover, it was considered desirable that Commander Skyrme should be interviewed before any police action was taken. The reason for this being that the cause of the trouble being what it was i.e., bad feeling between the cabin-boys and the newly promoted 2nd Steward it was thought that to arrest and charge the cabin-boys might result in a strike which would cause trouble and inconvenience to the Shipping Company, Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.
On the 28/7/37 D.S. Elders interviewed Commander Skyrme who requested that no Police action be taken until further word was received from him because the Stewards and Cabin-boys Unions were trying to settle the matter amicably among themselves.

Date June 25, 19 37.
Subject S.S. "Loongwo" - staff oppose the appointment of second steward.
Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by [Signature]

Unrest, as the result of the decision of the
management to appoint a boy of the s.s. "Tingwo" to act as
second steward, now exists among the 24 pantry-boys, 20 firemen,
18 sailors, 35 tallymen and 110 cabin boys of the Indo-China
S.N. Company's ship "Loongwo".

In connection with this matter, Mr. Yang Zuan-sung
(楊瑞生), a secretary of the Chinese Seamen's Union, called
at the company's office on the afternoon of June 24 and
discussed the situation with Commander Skyrme. The management,
however, refused to alter its decision.

At 9 p.m. June 24, the pantry boys of the s.s.
"Loongwo", at that time berthed at Hunt's Wharf, held a meeting
aboard the ship and decided that they would refuse to accept
the appointment of the new second steward, Hu Pao-tsao (胡宝棗). They
further stated that if the management insisted on his employ-
ment, they would, in company with the remainder of the crew,
declare a strike. Ringleaders and spokesmen at this meeting
were Pao Tao-fah (包道发) and Ah-ming (阿明), both pantry boys.

At 10.45 p.m. June 24, Mr. Yang Zuan-sung, in
company with Mr. Chen Yuen Ming (程永銘), Chief of the 2nd
Department of the Seamen's Union, boarded the steamer and
conveyed to the workers written instructions from General Yang
Hu to the effect that the newly appointed man should be allowed
to sail with the ship, that he should not be allowed to work
and that after one trip and on the vessel's return to Shanghai,
negotiations should be re-opened.

After much persuasion the pantry boys agreed to
comply with these instructions and without further incident
the s.s. "Loongwo" sailed at 12 m.n. June 24/25.

D.S. Henchman. 26/6

事由 “龙窝”轮（S.S. "Loongwo"）——职员反对任命第二管事。
制作人 D.S. Henchman 转呈人 [签名]

由于管理层决定任命一名原在“定窝”轮（s.s. "Tingwo"）服务的茶房侍者（boy）担任第二管事，印度支那轮船公司所属“龙窝”轮的24名配餐室侍者、20名生火员、18名水手、35名理货员和110名客舱侍者中出现了不安情绪。

就此事宜，中国海员工会秘书杨瑞生（Yang Zuan-sung）于6月24日下午前往公司办公室，与 Skyrme 指挥官讨论了局势。然而，管理层拒绝改变其决定。

6月24日晚9时，当时停泊于亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf）的“龙窝”轮上的配餐室侍者在船上举行会议，决定拒绝接受新任第二管事胡宝棗（Hu Pao-tsao）的任命。他们进一步表示，如果管理层坚持雇用他，他们将与其余船员一起宣布罢工。此次会议的带头人和发言人是两名配餐室侍者：包道发（Pao Tao-fah）和阿明（Ah-ming）。

6月24日晚10时45分，杨瑞生先生与中国海员工会第二部主任程永銘（Chen Yuen Ming）一同登上轮船，向工人们传达了杨虎将军的书面指示，大意是允许新任命的人员随船航行，但不允许其工作，待一个航次结束且船只返回上海后，应重新开启谈判。

经过多方劝说，配餐室侍者同意遵守这些指示，“龙窝”轮于6月24/25日午夜12时启航，未发生其他事件。

D.S. Henchman. 6月26日

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Threatened Strike of Stewards Employed
On Board The S.S. 'Loong Wu'.

During the late afternoon of June 24, Commander
F.H.E. Skyrme of Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd., reported
that he had received information to the effect that the
Chinese Stewards employed on board the S.S. 'Loong Wu'
which vessel is due to sail from Hunt's Wharf for Hankow
at 12 m.n. June 24, had threatened to go on strike if
the Company refused to accede to their demands and with-
draw from the ship's personnel one named Hu Pao Chu
(胡宝初) who has recently been appointed second steward
and transferred to the ship in this capacity in place
of one named Ying Chung Tuh (应忠德) who has been
promoted to chief steward and transferred from the
'Loong Wu' to another vessel.

Apparently the stewards had strongly objected to
Hu Pao Chu's appointment and claim that the position
vacated by Ying Chung Tuh should have been filled by
one of them and not an outsider.

The vessel sailed on schedule without any untoward
incident occurring.

A party of Uniform Police and detectives from
this Station under the supervision of a senior foreign
officer were on duty at the jetty until the vessel
sailed at 12 m.n.

（印：OFFICIAL RECORD 25 JUNE 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

Mr.
On May 28, Wong Zuan-ching (王喜慶), Chairman of
the Ewo River and Seagoing Steamers Saloon Employees' Mutual
Advantage Association, Lane 449, 27 East Seward Road, was
summoned by Mr. Bang Pah-wei (彭伯威), Chairman of the
Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union, to the latter's
office, 680 Chung Hwa Road, Nantao. He was requested to
resign from the Association because he had joined, it is alleged,
a secret reactionary group. To this request, Mr. Wong
agreed to comply.
At about 8 a.m. May 30, while he was in the vicinity
of the Association offices on East Seward Road, Mr. Wong was
set upon by three men armed with axes. He was, however,
fortunate enough to make good his escape without injury and
later reported the incident to the Hongkew Station.
(印：SPECIAL BRANCH - 7 JUNE 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE)
On June 1, Mr. Wong handed over the affairs of the
Association to the control of Mr. Yu Hwa-ziang (俞華祥),
a committee member of the Association, and left for his home
at Ningpo. It is learned that the Association has decided
to convene a general meeting of members on June 15 with a
view to electing new Chairman and committee members.
With regard to the reactionary group, of which Mr.
Wong is a member, further enquiries show that through the
introduction of Mr. Chao Sz-ching (趙世錦), a recently
dismissed clerk of the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Seamen's
Union, Mr. Wong became a member of a Special Service Group
of the Reorganization Party (Mr. Waung Ching-wei's party) with
a secret rendezvous at House 54, Mei Lai Faung (梅蘭坊), Rue
Amiral Bayle. Mr. Wong Shiao-ping, (王孝賓), ex-committee
member of the Shanghai Branch of the Seamen's Union, is said

先生，
5月28日，位于东熙华德路27弄449号的怡和江轮及海轮餐厅员工同益会主席王喜庆（Wong Zuan-ching），被中国海员工会上海分会主席彭伯威（Bang Pah-wei）召至其位于南市中华路680号的办公室。据称，因王喜庆加入了一个秘密反动团体，彭伯威要求其辞去在该会的职务。王喜庆同意照办。
5月30日上午8时许，当王喜庆在东熙华德路该会会所附近时，遭到三名手持斧头的男子袭击。然而，他幸运地未受伤并成功逃脱，随后向虹口警署报案。
（印：特务处 - 1937年6月7日 上海公共租界工部局警务处）
6月1日，王喜庆将该会事务移交给该会委员俞华祥（Yu Hwa-ziang）管理，并返回宁波家中。据悉，该会决定于6月15日召开会员大会，以选举新主席及委员会委员。
关于王喜庆所属的反动团体，进一步调查显示，通过最近被解雇的中国海员工会上海分会职员赵世锦（Chao Sz-ching）的介绍，王喜庆成为了重组派（汪精卫派）特别服务组的成员，其秘密联络点位于贝勒路梅兰坊54号。据说，前海员工会上海分会委员王孝宾（Wong Shiao-ping）负责

Subject Ewo Steamship Tallymen's Club - committee meeting.
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne D S I
The new committee members of the Ewo Steamship Tallymen's
Club, who were elected on April 11, 1937 (Vide I.R. 12.4.37),
held their first meeting in the offices of the Club, Lane 449,
No. 27 East Seward Road, between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. April 12,
when they formally assumed office. The following resolutions
were then discussed and passed:-
1. That unemployed tallymen be notified that in future when
seeking employment they should not apply to the companies
directly but to the Club which would recommend them.
2. That, in order to give opportunities for unemployed tallymen,
compradores of ships be requested not to engage apprentices.
3. That each member of the Club deposit with a certain bank
$3 a year for a period of five years, and that the sum thus
raised be transferred to the club and used for helping
unemployed members, etc. It is estimated that a sum of
about $1,000 could be raised yearly in this way.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

The above mentioned association, more commonly known as the
"Ewo Boys' Club," was officially inaugurated on 28 September,
1936 and became a registered subsidiary of the Shanghai Branch
of the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union. Closely
associated with the Boys' Club is the "Ewo Steamship Tallymen's
Club." Chairman Chen Yuen-loong (陈元龙), established in
1933 and also a subsidiary of the Shanghai Branch of the Chung
Hwa Seamen's Union.
Organiser of the "Boys' Club" was one Dzung Yah-chen
(郑协成), subsequently elected secretary. Dzung in soliciting
membership for his union is reported to have used threats and
coercion, and in carrying out these illegal activities is known
to have had the full support of Chen Yuen-loong who as well as
being chairman of the "Tallymen's Club," is also staff member
of the Shanghai Branch Office of the Chung Hwa Seamen's Union,
and is on very friendly terms with Pang Dah-wei (彭伯威) who
is said to be a favoured follower of General Yang Hu, Woosung-
Shanghai Defence Commissioner and concurrently Special
Kuomintang Delegate for Seamen's Affairs.
From the foregoing it would appear that the Kuomintang
and the Chung Hwa Seamen's Union anxious to assume complete
control over the Chinese staff of the Indo-China Steam
Navigation Company, in this instance the saloon boys in
particular, and prevented by law from officially inaugurating
a union, were actually behind and in full support of the
formation of the society known as the "Ewo Boys' Club." Much of
the friction, disturbance aboard ships, intimidation, etc. can be
said to have occurred directly or indirectly as a result of
the continued effort of the Chung Hwa Union, supported by the

上述协会，通称为“怡和少年俱乐部”，于1936年9月28日正式成立，并成为中华海员工会上海分会的注册附属机构。与少年俱乐部关系密切的是“怡和轮船理货员俱乐部”。主席陈元龙（Chen Yuen-loong），该会成立于1933年，亦为中华海员工会上海分会的附属机构。

“少年俱乐部”的组织者为郑协成（Dzung Yah-chen），后当选为秘书。据报道，郑协成在为其工会招募会员时使用了威胁和胁迫手段，而在进行这些非法活动时，众所周知得到了陈元龙的全力支持。陈元龙除担任“理货员俱乐部”主席外，还是中华海员工会上海办事处的工作人员，并与彭伯威（Pang Dah-wei）（音译）关系非常友好。据说彭伯威是杨虎将军的亲信追随者，杨虎任吴淞上海防卫专员，并兼任国民党海员事务特别代表。

从前述情况看来，国民党和中华海员工会急于完全控制印度支那轮船公司（Indo-China Steam Navigation Company）的中国职员，特别是本案中的餐厅侍者（saloon boys），但因法律限制无法正式成立工会，实际上是在背后全力支持名为“怡和少年俱乐部”的社团的成立。可以说，船上的许多摩擦、骚乱、恐吓等事件，都是中华海员工会在

In August, 1935 the comprador of the s.s. "Suiwo" was threatened

In July, 1936 Chung Yah-chen, secretary of the Boys' Club,

that those who refused would be dealt with by the San Huh
Wei (三合会), a Cantonese loafers' club. In consequence
of this 22 boys and cooks of the s.s. "Pingwo" registered
with the union.
Again in July, 1936 when a vacancy occurred for the position
of No.1 Cook on the s.s. "Suiwo," the "Boys' Club" refused to
accept the company's nominee and with the approval of the Chung
Hwa Seamen's Union installed their own candidate.
Further instance in July, 1936: two saloon boys (union members)
of the "Pingwo" dismissed by the Captain for absence without
permission. Union Representatives, including Chen Yuen-loong,
accompanied by loafers boarded the "Pingwo" and threatened the
second steward with a view to reinstating the saloon boys.
In January, 1937, representatives of the "Boys' Club," including
Wong Zoen-ching (王善慶), the chairman, boarded the s.s.
"Kutwo" and threatening to bring about the dismissal of those
who refused, attempted to induce non-members to join their union.

1936年7月，少年俱乐部秘书郑协成（Chung Yah-chen）登上“平和”轮（s.s. "Pingwo"），要求所有餐厅侍者、厨房工作人员等加入其工会，并威胁称拒绝者将受到三合会（San Huh Wei），一个广东游民团体的处置。因此，“平和”轮的22名侍者和厨师在工会进行了登记。

On 4th Feb.1937, as the result of an attempt by the company to
dismiss certain of its tallymen (union men), a fight occurred
aboard the s.s. "Prominent" while at sea and the vessel was
forced to put back to Shanghai. Chen Yuen-loong who disapproved
of the company's action in dismissing the tallymen, is believed
to have been responsible of the trouble. On 16th Feb.1937,
friction was caused aboard the s.s. "Kungwo" when the tallymen
attempted to usurp certain privileges claimed as their right
by the sailors. A settlement was however affected.
On 19th February, 1937, the respective stewards of the s.s.
"Kiawo" and s.s. "Kungwo" wished to change ships, this with
the company's approval. The cooks, who would have been
transferred with their respective stewards, supported by the
saloon boys opposed the change and Chen Yuen-loong, at the
instigation of Pang Bah-wei, informed the stewards that if they
made the change they would be penalised by the union.
On 26th Feb. 1937, S.M.P. Special Branch H.Q. received a
message from the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company stating
that because six saloon boys of the s.s. "Pingwo" had resigned
from the "Ewo Boys' Club," trouble might be expected. On 12th
March, information was received that the six saloon boys had
been arrested by the Chinese authorities in Nantao. It appears
that the boys were requested to visit the offices of the
Chung Hwa Seamen's Union in Nantao. This they did and on
arrival were questioned as to their reasons for resigning from
the "Ewo Boys' Club." Their answers were apparently unsatis-
factory from the point of view of the union officials and a

1937年2月4日，由于公司试图解雇某些理货员（工会成员），“显赫”轮（s.s. "Prominent"）在海上发生斗殴，迫使该船返回上海。陈元龙不赞成公司解雇理货员的举动，被认为应对此次骚乱负责。1937年2月16日，当理货员试图篡夺水手声称是其权利的特权时，“公和”轮（s.s. "Kungwo"）上发生了摩擦。然而，此事得以解决。

1937年2月19日，“交和”轮（s.s. "Kiawo"）和“公和”轮的各自大副希望调换船只，此举得到了公司的批准。本应随各自大副调动的厨师，在餐厅侍者的支持下反对这一变动，陈元龙在彭伯威（Pang Bah-wei）（音译）的唆使下通知大副们，如果他们进行调动，将受到工会的惩罚。

1937年2月26日，工部局警务处特别支部总部收到印度支那轮船公司的消息，称由于“平和”轮的六名餐厅侍者退出了“怡和少年俱乐部”，预计可能会发生麻烦。3月12日，收到情报称这六名餐厅侍者已被中国当局在南市逮捕。看来，这些侍者被要求前往南市的中华海员工会办事处。他们照办了，到达后被问及退出“怡和少年俱乐部”的原因。从工会官员的角度来看，他们的回答显然不能令人满意，于是

dispute arose which resulted in the arrest of the boys. They
were charged with creating a disturbance and assaulting Chen
Yung-ming (陳允明 ), a departmental chief of the union,
and were detained on the authorization of General Yang Hu,
at the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters,

The foregoing instances show clearly that the "Two Boys'
Club" and the "Two Tallymen's Club," with the support of the
Chung Hwa Seamen's Union and General Yang Hu are not acting
in the best interests of the employees but seem rather, regardless
of what methods they employ, to be interested only in
increasing their influence over the Company's Chinese staff.
Attached to this report are copies of letters which form
part of a correspondence which has been carried on between
the Indo-China S.N.Co. Ltd. and General Yang Hu concerning
the activities of the "Two Boys' Club." Perusal will show
quite clearly the attitude of the Union towards the Company
and in particular its disregard of the necessity for
discipline aboard the Company's ships; per ex. quoting from
a letter dated 26th Nov. 1936, written by General Yang Hu
and addressed to the Company; General Yang Hu states: "Save the
orders by the Captain, who has the highest authority on his
ship, the crew is not necessary to obey all the commands
of other officers, because after all, they are not slaves."
A copy of a letter from the Indo-China S.N. Company,
Ltd. to Sir John Brenan containing a memorandum on the
activities of the Boys' Club, is also attached.

发生了争执，导致侍者们被捕。他们被指控制造骚乱并袭击工会部门主管陈允明（Chen Yung-ming），并经杨虎将军授权，拘押于龙华吴淞上海卫戍司令部。3月19日，在被拘留七天后，这些餐厅侍者获保释释放。

上述实例清楚地表明，“怡和少年俱乐部”和“怡和理货员俱乐部”在中华海员工会和杨虎将军的支持下，并非为了员工的最佳利益行事，而是似乎不顾采用何种手段，只关心增加其对公司中国职员的影响力。

本报告附有信件副本，这些信件构成了印度支那轮船有限公司与杨虎将军之间关于“怡和少年俱乐部”活动的通信的一部分。阅读这些信件将清楚地显示工会对公司的态度，特别是其无视公司船上纪律必要性的态度；例如，引用杨虎将军于1936年11月26日写给公司的一封信中的话，杨虎将军称：“除了拥有船上最高权威的船长的命令外，船员没有必要服从其他军官的所有命令，因为毕竟，他们不是奴隶。”

另附有一封印度支那轮船有限公司致约翰·布伦南爵士（Sir John Brenan）的信函副本，其中包含一份关于少年俱乐部活动的备忘录。

特别支部副主任。
J. Bencliman D. P. S.

The Indo-China Steam Navigation Co. Ltd
(INCORPORATED IN ENGLAND)
JARDINE, MATHESON & CO., LTD.
GENERAL MANAGERS.
SHANGHAI
March 23rd, 1937.

The Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Foochow Road,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

Referring to the case of six boys of our domestic staff who were arrested by the Shanghai Branch of the Seamen's Union with the details of which you are acquainted, we are somewhat apprehensive as to the safety of these men. We attach a list of their names and addresses with a request that, if possible, some supervision might be exercised over them.

These boys resigned voluntarily from the Ewo Boy's Club which has its Office in Seward Road, Hongkew, and we have no doubt that, had they escaped the punishment of imprisonment which they had to suffer, it would have encouraged at least 60% of the remaining boys of our domestic staff to act in a similar way. We know that the Officers of the Ewo Boy's Club bring intimidating pressure to bear on our staff and, for the good of all concerned, we are convinced that it is a bad influence in every way.

The Club is supported by the Ewo Tallymen's Club situated in the same building and this also has a bad influence in support of which we quote the recent fight of tallymen on board s.s. "Prominent" and a certain fracas which took place between sailors and tallymen of s.s. "Kungwo" on approximately January 15th.

We believe that the headquarters of the Seamen's Union would be glad to see the end of the Ewo Boy's Club and we, ourselves, would be glad to see the end of both the Ewo Boy's Club and Ewo Tallymen's Club which are a constant source of irritation to us and seriously interfere with the good management of our ships and our service to the public.

We would be more than obliged if some action on your part could bring about the suppression of one or both of these organisations.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,
Jardine Matheson and Co. Ltd
General Managers. Indo-China S. N. Co. Ltd.

尊敬的先生：

我们相信海员工会总部也乐于看到怡和少年俱乐部的终结，而我们自己也乐于看到怡和少年俱乐部和怡和理货员俱乐部两者的终结，因为它们不断引起我们的烦恼，并严重干扰了我们船舶的良好管理以及对公众的服务。

如果阁下的行动能够促成取缔其中一个或两个组织，我们将不胜感激。

此致，
敬礼，

Copy of letter from the General Manager of the Indo-China
S.N. Co. to Sir John Brenan, K.C.M.G., H.B.M. Consul General,
Shanghai.

Shanghai,
January 13, 1937.

Sir.

We have the honour to submit the following memor-
andum on the activities of the Chinese Seamen's Union at
Shanghai.

For some months past there has been a decided
tendency on the part of certain Branches of the Chinese
Seamen's Union to conduct a campaign of lawlessness and in-
subordination which is subversive of discipline on board
ship and, unless firmly checked, will doubtless result in
serious accidents. Our efforts to adjust these matters
are always met with threats, broken promises, and in some
cases, violence.

On November 4th the Headquarters of the Union
issued an edict stating, among other things, that the orders
of the Captain of the ship must be strictly obeyed.

We pointed out in our letter dated November 10th
that the Captain necessarily delegates his authority to
his subordinates including the Chinese heads of departments.
The Union, in their reply dated November 26th, declared
that they did not consider it necessary for the men to obey
the orders of anyone but the Captain.

This is an example of the attitude of the Union
and, in itself, should be the cause for very strong repre-
sentation.

Further than this, however, we can show that even
the Captain's orders are treated with disrespect by a certain
Branch of the Union, viz. the Saloon Staff.

The disaffection of this Department is a compara-
tively new venture though we can quote an example of attempt-
ed interference in the lawful dismissal of a fireman for
gross neglect of duty and the troubles with the teaboys,
tallymen, etc. are too well known to be enlarged upon.

We have written to General Yang Hu, the Commission-
er in charge of the National Seamen's Union, requesting an
interview so that the situation can be explained personally
to him. This, however, has produced no result - not even
an official acknowledgment. We are of the opinion that
his subordinates do not wish him to be acquainted with the
facts. A copy of our letter (December 24th) to him request-
ing an interview is attached and also the letter dated Dec-
ember 3rd which we propose to read to him personally.

This last letter summarises the situation with re-
gard to our Saloon Staff.

印度支那轮船公司（Indo-China S.N. Co.）总经理致大英帝国驻上海总领事约翰·布伦南爵士（Sir John Brenan, K.C.M.G.）的信件副本。

上海，
1937年1月13日。

先生：

谨呈上关于上海中国海员工会活动情况的备忘录如下。

过去数月来，中国海员工会的某些分会明显倾向于开展一场违法和不服从管束的运动，这破坏了船上的纪律，如果不坚决加以制止，无疑会导致严重事故。我们为解决这些问题所做的努力，总是遭到威胁、违背承诺，在某些情况下甚至遭遇暴力。

11月4日，该工会总部发布了一项命令，其中规定必须严格遵守船长的指令。

我们在11月10日的信中指出，船长必然将其权力下放给其下属，包括华籍各部门主管。工会在11月26日的回函中宣称，他们认为船员没有必要服从除船长以外的任何人的命令。

这是工会态度的一个例证，其本身就应该成为提出强烈交涉的理由。

此外，我们还可以证明，即使是船长的命令，也受到工会某一特定分会——即餐厅职员分会（Saloon Staff）——的蔑视。

该部门的不满情绪是相对较新的现象，尽管我们可以举出一个例子，即试图干涉因严重失职而合法解雇一名司炉工的行为，而与茶房侍者（teaboys）、理货员（tallymen）等发生的纠纷已众所周知，无需赘述。

我们已致信负责全国海员工会的杨虎将军，请求面谈，以便向他亲自说明情况。然而，此举未产生任何结果——甚至连官方的确认回复都没有。我们认为，他的下属不希望他了解事实真相。随函附上我们于12月24日致信请求面谈的副本，以及我们拟当面向他宣读的12月3日的信件。

最后一封信概括了关于我们餐厅职员的情况。

Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.,
Shanghai, December 31, 1936.

General Yang Hu,
Chinese Seamen's Union.
Mantao.

Dear Sir,

We wish to call your attention to two cases of assault by
members of the Seamen's Union on fellow-members; namely, Stewards
of s.s. "Pingwo" and s.s. "Pausang". From our previous
experience it would appear that this is one of the rules of the
Union which is strictly enforced and the men concerned should be
dismissed from membership of the Union and consequently from
our employment.

We quote first from the report of the Captain of
s.s. "Pingwo" :-

"Yesterday afternoon (26th Dec), as a result of the
incitement of other "B" Saloon boys who have similarly been
entirely unsatisfactory and under whose influence Chan Yue
Yao seems to be, Chan Yue Yao, after an hysterical outburst
which could be heard practically all over the ship, was
induced to assault the Steward in his cabin.

"The Chief Officer, Mr. A.E. Smith, was witness to
part of this affair, but in view of the peculiar circum-
stances, refrained from interference. The Chinese handled the
affairs themselves.

"The Chief Steward has exhibited wonderful tolerance in
the face of perpetual insolence and baiting which has been
indulged in of late by all these saloon boys associated with
the two who deserted some time ago. He is one of the best
Stewards, both as caterer and in service to passengers, who
it has been my fortune to be shipmates with in the Company."

We endorse the Captain's remarks about the excellence
of this Steward and would point out that the two boys referred
to by the Captain are the ones for whom we hold your guarantee
of good behaviour.

We are suspending Chan Yue Yao from service pending
investigation of the case on the return of s.s. "Pingwo" to
Shanghai on Monday, the 4th instant.

We now refer to the case of s.s. "Pausang". Attached
is the statement of the Chief Officer which gives the details
of the assault. The Captain was asked to make a report and he
quotes many instances of dirtiness, slovenliness and inattention
to duty on the part of the domestic staff, saying :-

"During the whole of this period up to date there
have been numerous occasions when I have had to speak
severely to the Steward over the following :-

attending officers, wireless operator, and even

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理致中国海员工会杨虎将军的信件副本
------------------

印度支那轮船公司，
上海，1936年12月31日。

杨虎将军，
中国海员工会。
曼涛（Mantao，音译）。

亲爱的先生：

我们要提请您注意两起海员工会成员殴打同事的案件；即“平沃”号（s.s. "Pingwo"）和“宝山”号（s.s. "Pausang"）的大副（Steward，此处指餐厅总管/大管事）。根据我们以往的经验，这似乎是工会严格执行的规则之一，相关人员应被开除出工会会员资格，从而也被解除我们的雇佣关系。

首先引用“平沃”号船长的报告：

“昨天下午（12月26日），在其他同样表现极差的‘B’舱餐厅男孩的煽动下，陈耀尧（Chan Yue Yao，音译）似乎受其影响，在一阵几乎全船都能听到的歇斯底里的爆发后，被诱导在其舱房内袭击了大副（Steward）。

“大副A.E.史密斯先生目睹了部分事件，但鉴于情况特殊，未加干涉。华人自行处理了此事。

“面对近来所有这些与不久前逃跑的两人有关的餐厅男孩所表现的持续无礼和挑衅，首席大副（Chief Steward）表现出了惊人的容忍度。他是本公司中我所幸与之共事过的最优秀的餐厅大副之一，无论是在餐饮供应还是乘客服务方面。”

我们赞同船长对这位大副优秀表现的评价，并指出船长提到的那两个男孩正是由贵方担保行为良好的人员。

在“平沃”号于本月4日星期一返回上海并对案件进行调查期间，我们将暂停陈耀尧的工作。

现在我们提及“宝山”号的案件。随函附上大副的陈述，其中详细说明了袭击情况。船长被要求提交报告，他列举了家务人员肮脏、邋遢和玩忽职守的许多实例，称：

“在此期间直至目前，我不得不就以下问题严厉训斥大副多次：
男孩们在配餐室喧哗和讨论，男孩们伺候高级船员、无线电操作员，甚至

Finally this has culminated in personal assaults
on two of our Chief Stewards as described in our letter dated
December 31st attached. In both these cases such inti-
midation was brought to bear as to frighten the Stewards
from performing their duties by sailing in the ships.

Certain Regulations (attached) were drawn up and
reply by the Chinese Seamen's Union is attached. On one
point in particular we have not yet come to an understand-
ing, viz. paragraph 5. We would be prepared to agree on
this point too but our experience over the past few months
has been such as to discredit entirely the good faith of
the Union who, so far from supporting us in the dismissal of
offenders, exert all their powers to protect them.

Now almost every clause of the Agreement has been
violated.

1. The cases of assault on the Stewards of s.s.
"Faushang" and s.s. "Pingwo".

3. Installation of one topass in s.s. "Kungwo" without
reference to the General Managers. This man is
still on board but is not on the Articles or in
receipt of pay.

4. a) Promotion of boys in s.s. "Kungwo" who are
eligible neither by long service or good
conduct.

b) Refusal to allow exchange of staff to be
effected on proposed exchange of Stewards
of s.s. "Kungwo" and s.s. "Kiawo".

6. Staff taking leave without permission or going
through the proper channels.

Paragraphs 2 and 7 have not yet been put into effect
pending a satisfactory settlement of the domestic affairs
generally.

All the above would appear to be a quarrel between
the Stewards - who are members of the Seamen's Union but not
the Ewo Boy's Club - and their Staffs but it is obvious that
the results of this state of affairs will be far-reaching.

We therefore request that the matter may be taken
up officially so that we may have an opportunity to explain
our case personally to General Yang Hu and point out to
him that we are willing to co-operate for the benefit of
our employees and the general public whom we serve.

We have the honour to be,

Sir,

Your obedient servants,

General Managers. Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd.

Sir John Brenan, K.C.M.G.

H.B.M. Consul General,

Shanghai.

最终，这演变成对我们两位首席大副的人身攻击，如随附的12月31日信件中所述。在这两起案件中，施加了如此程度的恐吓，致使大副们因恐惧而在船上履行职责时感到害怕。

制定了一些规章（见附件），中国海员工会的回复也附在后面。特别是在某一点上，我们尚未达成一致，即第5段。我们也准备在此点上达成协议，但过去几个月的经验使我们完全怀疑工会的诚意，他们非但不支持我们解雇违规者，反而动用一切权力保护他们。

现在，协议的几乎每一条款都遭到了违反。

1. 袭击“福生”号（s.s. "Faushang"）和“平沃”号（s.s. "Pingwo"）大副的案件。

3. 未经总经理批准，在“公和”号（s.s. "Kungwo"）上安装一名通事（topass）。此人仍在船上，但未列入船员名单，也未领取薪水。

4. a) 提升“公和”号上既无长期服务资历也无良好品行资格的男孩。

b) 拒绝允许在提议交换“公和”号和“嘉禾”号（s.s. "Kiawo"）的大副时进行人员调换。

6. 工作人员未经许可或未通过适当渠道擅自休假。

第2和第7段尚未生效，有待家务事务总体得到满意解决。

以上所有情况看似是餐厅大副（他们是海员工会成员，但不是怡和男孩俱乐部 Ewo Boy's Club 的成员）与其下属之间的争执，但显然这种局势的后果将是深远的。

因此，我们请求正式处理此事，以便我们有机会向杨虎将军亲自解释我们的立场，并向他指出，为了我们的雇员和我们所服务的公众的利益，我们愿意合作。

此致，

敬礼

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理

约翰·布伦南爵士，K.C.M.G.

大英帝国驻上海总领事，

上海。

副本

案件摘要

1. 8月7日，怡和男孩俱乐部成员在流浪汉协助下袭击“新昌和”号（s.s. "Hsin Changwo"）大副。

2. 强制复职某些故意弃船的男孩，涉及“公和”号、“平沃”号和“宝和”号（s.s. "Paowo"）。参见8月18日致您的信件。

3. 尽管有书面协议和工会秘书黄克耀（K.Y. Wong，音译）先生的个人承诺，“公和”号一案仍违背诺言。参见我们11月10日的信件。
a) 不增加我方员工人数。
b) 按资历和服务优良程度晋升人员。

4. 袭击和恐吓“耀生”号（s.s. "Yausang"）和“平沃”号的大副。参见我们12月31日的信件。

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from the Chief Officer of the S.S. Fausang
to General Managers of the Jardine, Matheson & Co.

s.s. "Fausang"
Shanghai, Dec. 25th, 1936.

Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co.
General Managers.

Dear Sirs,

During the evening of Dec. 23rd at Shanghai, it
was reported to me that there was trouble between the Steward
and pantry boys, which was developing into a fight.

On going to the saloon to investigate the matter,
I found the Steward surrounded by menacing saloon boys and
about half a dozen of their Trades Union friends from ashore.
One of the latter took it upon himself to settle the dispute
with me.

On asking him if he was a Union Official and to
produce his card, he said he could not do so, as he was
only acting in the capacity of a middleman. Whereupon I
declined to discuss ship's business with him as it was
no concern of his.

This ended the row for the time being; but the
Steward afterwards told me that he wished to leave the ship,
in spite of having been here for ten years, as his position
was becoming impossible.

The matter was duly reported to the Captain on the
following morning.

I remain, dear Sir,
Your obedient servant,

D. Bernhard-Smith.

Chief Officer.
page_data.zh:
“福生”号（S.S. Fausang）大副致怡和洋行（Jardine, Matheson & Co.）总经理的信件副本

“福生”号
上海，1936年12月25日。

怡和洋行
总经理。

尊敬的先生们：

12月23日晚在上海，有人向我报告，大副与配餐室男孩之间发生纠纷，并正演变为斗殴。

当我前往餐厅调查此事时，发现大副被具有威胁性的餐厅男孩包围，还有大约六名来自岸上的工会朋友。其中一人自作主张要与我解决争端。

当我问他是否是工会官员并要求出示证件时，他说他无法出示，因为他只是以中间人的身份行事。于是，我拒绝与他讨论船务，因为这与他的职责无关。

这场争吵暂时平息；但大副后来告诉我，尽管他已在此工作十年，但他希望离开这艘船，因为他的处境已变得无法忍受。

此事已于次日早晨 duly 向船长报告。

此致，

敬礼

D. Bernhard-Smith.

大副。

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from General Managers, Indo-China S.N.
Co. to General Yang Hu, Shanghai-Woosung Garrison
Headquarters.

Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.
Shanghai, Dec. 24, 1936.

General Yang Hu,
Shanghai-Woosung Garrison Headquarters,
Lunghwa.

Dear Sir,

We fully realise that, in this time of National
Crisis, the important position which you hold must increase
your duties considerably and you can spare little time to
matters other than those of immediate national consequence.
Yet we feel that the matter we wish to lay before you is
of great importance and, if not dealt with immediately and
firmly, may have far-reaching repercussions. We refer to the
employment of loafers and other bad characters on the wharves
by certain Branches of the Seamen's Union to enforce their
demands by creating disturbances on board our ships.

We have tried all reasonable methods of negotiations
to reach an understanding with the representatives of the
union and we regret that we can get no satisfaction.

We therefore beg leave to visit you personally:
so that we can lay our case before you with confidence that
justice will be done. We make this request because the
nature of the case is too involved to put on paper without
the chance of misunderstanding which we wish to avoid,
trusting that you will be able to fix an early date for an
interview.

We should like to make it clear that it is our wish
to do all we can, ourselves, to maintain order and discipline
on our ships and wharves and you can count on our full support
in this connection.

We take this opportunity of wishing you the
compliments of the season with the hope of a speedy solution
to the troubles in which your country is at present involved.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,

General Managers, Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd.
page_data.zh:
印度支那轮船公司总经理致上海吴淞要塞司令部杨虎将军的信件副本。

印度支那轮船公司
上海，1936年12月24日。

杨虎将军，
上海吴淞要塞司令部，
龙华。

亲爱的先生：

我们充分认识到，在这个国家危机时刻，您所担任的重要职位必然使您的职责大大增加，您几乎没有时间处理除直接关乎国家大事以外的事务。然而，我们觉得我们要向您陈述的事情非常重要，如果不立即果断处理，可能会产生深远的影响。我们指的是海员工会某些分会雇佣码头上的流浪汉和其他不良分子，通过在我們的船上制造骚乱来强行推行他们的要求。

我们已尝试所有合理的谈判方法以与工会代表达成共识，但遗憾的是未能获得满意的结果。

因此，我们恳请获准亲自拜访您：以便我们能自信地向您陈述我们的案情，相信正义会得到伸张。我们提出这一请求是因为案件性质过于复杂，诉诸笔端难免产生误解，而我们希望避免这种情况，相信您能尽早安排面谈日期。

我们要澄清的是，我们希望尽己所能维持船只和码头的秩序与纪律，在此方面您可以指望我们的全力支持。

借此机会，祝您节日愉快，并希望贵国目前卷入的麻烦能迅速得到解决。

此致，

敬礼

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from General Managers, Indo-China S.N. Co.
to General Yang Hu, Chinese Seamen's Union, Nantao

.........

Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.
Shanghai, December 3rd, 1936.

General Yang Hu,
Chinese Seamen's Union
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

It is only after trying all means to reach a
satisfactory agreement with your Representatives that we take
this step of approaching you personally on a matter of the
utmost importance.

It is a question of good discipline which you, as
an Officer, can fully understand.

We regret to inform you that a certain Branch of
the Seamen's Union at Shanghai called the Ewo Boy's Club,
under the leadership of one, Chen Yuen-loong, who is
Chairman of the Ewo Tallymen's Club, has been formed with
the admitted purpose of resisting the authority of the Chief
Stewards of our ships and consequently the Captain of the
ship who delegates his authority through his Officers to
the heads of Departments. This is directly contrary to the
spirit of the Decree issued by yourself and the results,
if the activities of the Club are allowed to continue, will
be a general undermining of all discipline, not only in
the ships of our company, but internationally in all ships
trading to this Port. The repercussions are bound to be
far-reaching.

We have had several meetings with your Represent-
atives on this subject and our relations have been most
cordial. Still, however, in spite of our agreements we find
the activities of the club in progress and we can only
assume that they carry on without the knowledge of their
superiors. Their methods are to employ loafers on the wharves
to enforce their demands and this has led in some cases to
physical violence, particularly in the case of s.s. "Hsin
Changwo" last July when the Chief Steward was only rescued
by the intervention of the ship's officers and the summoning
of the Police. We are glad, however, to inform you that
we have agreed with your Representatives that they will take
the responsibility for the summoning of Police assistance
in future.

The grounds on which the Ewo Boy's Club bases
its policy of insubordination appears to be that the Stewards
dismiss and employ their staff indiscriminately. For a year
now we have been taking particular interest in our Saloon
Passenger Department and one of our efforts has been to
exercise an adequate supervision over our employees in this
Department to see that they were justly treated and gained
their promotion by long service and good conduct.
page_data.zh:
印度支那轮船公司（Indo-China S.N. Co.）总经理致中国海员工会杨虎将军函副本，地址：南市

.........

印度支那轮船公司
上海，1936年12月3日。

致：
中国海员工会
杨虎将军
上海。

尊敬的先生：

只有在尝试了各种手段均未能与贵方代表达成令人满意的协议之后，我们才采取这一步骤，就一件至关重要的事项直接与您本人联系。

这是一个关于良好纪律的问题，作为一位军官，您能够充分理解这一点。

我们遗憾地通知您，上海海员工会的一个分支，名为“怡和侍者俱乐部”（Ewo Boy's Club），在怡和理货员俱乐部主席陈元龙（Chen Yuen-loong，音译）的领导下已经成立，其公开目的是抵制我方船舶大副的权威，进而抵制通过其下属官员将权力授予各部门主管的船长。这直接违背了您本人颁布的法令精神，如果允许该俱乐部的活动继续下去，其结果将是全面破坏所有纪律，不仅影响我公司的船舶，而且会影响国际上所有往来本港的船舶。其反响必然是深远的。

我们就此问题与贵方代表举行了多次会议，双方关系最为融洽。然而，尽管达成了协议，我们发现该俱乐部的活动仍在进行，我们只能推测这些活动是在其上级不知情的情况下进行的。他们的手段是雇佣码头上的闲散人员来强制执行他们的要求，这在某些情况下导致了肢体暴力，特别是去年七月在“新昌沃”号（s.s. "Hsin Changwo"，音译）轮上发生的事件，当时大副仅在船员的干预和报警后才得以脱险。不过，我们很高兴地通知您，我们已与贵方代表达成协议，他们将负责在未来请求警方协助。

“怡和侍者俱乐部”将其不服从政策基于的理由似乎是，大副随意解雇和雇用其员工。一年来，我们一直特别关注我们的头等舱客运部门，我们的努力之一是对该部门的员工进行适当的监督，以确保他们受到公正对待，并通过长期服务和良好表现获得晋升。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

It is only since we introduced this practice that
the troubles with our Staff began and we now find out, far
from just treatment, the Ewo Boy's Club takes it upon itself
to protect wrong-doers and to endeavour to promote members
of the staff who are qualified neither by long service nor
good conduct.

Their latest action has been to refuse to allow the
Stewards - also members of the Seamen's Union, be it noted -
to participate in the share of passenger's tips. Although
we do not recognise these tips and it is no concern of ours,
yet this sort of behaviour must cause illfeeling which we
understand it is your object to avoid.

We came to an agreement on the 17th November with your
Representatives on the following points :-

1. The settlement of a certain disturbance in s.s. "Kungwo",
the details of which are briefly described in the
attached appendix.

2. That dealings between ourselves and our Staff would be
through the Union Headquarters and not through the Ewo
Boy's Club.

3. That internal arrangement, appointment and promotion of
Staff in ships would be left in our hands and worked from
a roster of service which we keep.

4. That in the event of new employees being required they
would be taken from a list of our exemployees a copy
of which would be sent to the Union.

5. That we should summon Police assistance in case of any
disturbance from the direction of Ewo Boys Club and
that the Union would take the responsibility/

We regret to say that the first clause of the
agreement has not been complied with and it shakes our faith in
the fulfilment of the remaining clauses. For this reason we
have taken it upon ourselves to approach you direct and to
ask that you will be good enough to use your influence in
the suppression of the activities of this Ewo Boy's Club.
Otherwise, as we have said before, we fear that a state of
undiscipline will run through our Fleet with consequent danger
to ships involving loss of life and property which will be
readily traced to the bad influence of certain Branches of the
Seamen's Union.

All this, as you can readily understand, is
particularly important, in the case of ships where good
discipline is essential. Not only will any cases of in-
subordination be immediately noticeable by the travelling
public, but there will be every danger of a serious
accident which would undoubtedly have world-wide publicity.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,

General Managers. Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

只有在我们引入这一做法后，与我们员工的麻烦才开始出现，而现在我们发现，“怡和侍者俱乐部”非但没有提供公正待遇，反而擅自保护违规者，并试图提拔那些既无长期服务经历也无良好表现的员工。

他们最近的行动是拒绝允许大副——顺便提一句，他们也是海员工会的成员——参与分享乘客的小费。虽然我们不承认这些小费，且这与我们要无关，但此类行为必然引起不和，而我们理解这是您希望避免的。

我们在11月17日与贵方代表就以下几点达成了协议：-

1. 解决“公和”号（s.s. "Kungwo"，音译）轮上发生的某起骚乱，详情简要描述于附件附录中。

2. 我方与我方员工之间的交涉将通过工会总部进行，而不是通过“怡和侍者俱乐部”。

3. 船上员工的内部安排、任命和晋升将由我方掌握，并根据我方保存的服务名册进行操作。

4. 如果需要新员工，将从我方前员工名单中录用，该名单副本将发送给工会。

5. 如果“怡和侍者俱乐部”方面发生任何骚乱，我们将请求警方协助，并由工会承担责任/

我们遗憾地说，协议的第一条并未得到遵守，这动摇了我们对履行剩余条款的信心。因此，我们不得不直接与您联系，恳请您运用您的影响力，取缔“怡和侍者俱乐部”的活动。否则，正如我们之前所说，我们担心这种无纪律状态将蔓延至我们的整个船队，从而给船舶带来危险，涉及生命和财产损失，而这很容易追溯到海员工会某些分支的不良影响。

所有这些，如您能轻易理解的那样，在那些良好纪律至关重要的船舶上尤为重要。任何不服从的情况不仅会立即被旅行公众注意到，而且极有可能发生严重事故，这无疑会引起全球性的关注。

尊敬的先生，
此致，

敬礼

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

December 3, 1936.

P.S.

Since writing the foregoing we have received a
letter from your Union dated 26th November in reply to our
comments on your decree.

We pointed out that the Captain of a ship necessarily
delegated his authority to his subordinates and suggested that the
decree, stating that only the Captain and the Purser could give
orders which must be obeyed, should be amended.

The letter from your Union dated 26th November
stated that they did not consider it necessary for the crew
to obey commands from anyone else. It is surely not necessary
to remark further on this to an Officer of your experience.

General Managers. Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

1936年12月3日。

附言：

在撰写上述内容后，我们收到了贵工会于11月26日发出的信函，回复我们就您法令提出的意见。

我们指出，船长必然将其权力下放给其下属官员，并建议修改该法令，其中规定只有船长和大副发出的命令才必须服从。

贵工会11月26日的信函表示，他们认为船员没有必要服从其他任何人的命令。对于像您这样经验丰富的军官来说，确实无需对此再多作评论。

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理。

page_data.en:
COPY

CASE OF S.S. "KUNGWO"

The Chief Officer retired and his personal
servant, who had been many years in the Company, retired
with him.

Instead of allowing the new Chief Officer to
choose his own servant, the Ewo Boy's Club took it upon
themselves to promote from the "B" Saloon a boy who is
recommended neither by long service nor good conduct (he
having absented himself from the ship twice without
permission of the Captain). Furthermore, they promoted
the lavatory and bath attendant to be a Saloon Boy and
brought in his place another man of whose antecedents we
know nothing and who, we have reason to suspect, is not
a good character owing to his connection with the Ewo
Boy's Club.

It was agreed with your Representatives, who were
not aware of the action of the Ewo Boy's Club, to revert
these men to their former positions pending settlement. This
agreement, we regret to say, has not been carried out.

December 3rd, 1936.
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
副本

“公和”号（S.S. "KUNGWO"）案例

大副退休，他在公司服务多年的私人仆役也随他一同退休。

“怡和侍者俱乐部”没有让新任大副选择自己的仆役，而是擅自从“B”等舱提升了一名男孩，此人既无长期服务经历，也无良好表现（他曾两次未经船长许可擅离船舶）。此外，他们将厕所和浴室服务员提升为头等舱侍者，并引入了另一名男子顶替其位置，我们对这名男子的背景一无所知，但有理由怀疑，由于他与“怡和侍者俱乐部”的关系，他的人品不佳。

经与贵方代表协商——他们当时并不知晓“怡和侍者俱乐部”的行动——同意将这些人员恢复原职，以待问题解决。我们遗憾地说，该协议并未得到执行。

1936年12月3日。
上海。

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from Yang Hu, Chinese Seamen's Union, to
Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd.
----------

Chinese Seamen's Union,
West Gate, Shanghai

November 26, 1936.

Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co.

Dear Sirs,

With reference to your letter of the 10th November
asking us to amend article 4 of our notification, we beg to point
out to you that the nature of that notification is to warn our
fellow members from doing any unlawful acts. It is by no means
an oppression on the workmen.

Save the orders by the Captain, who has the highest
authority on his ship, the crew is not necessary to obey all the
commands of other officers, because after all, they are not slaves.

You are dissatisfied with a certain section of your
employees, you therefore disapprove with our circular letter.
As to the "Tung Yih Club" it is formed by the staff of the Steward
department of different ships with an object of promoting good
feeling amongst themselves. It may help your business if you have
enough confidence in it. Through our investigation, we find that
the said club is looked upon as a hazardous organization because your
Mr. Ma, the Chief Steward, and a rascal named Li are trying various
ways of spoiling it in a view to form another organization of
their interest.

We wrote in your letter that one Wang Sin Ching brought
a gang of rascals to force upon the employing of certain workmen.
As Wang Sin Ching is a responsible member of the "Tung Yih Club"
and at the same time a very honest person, we cannot believe that
he would have such a thing like this.

We also can hardly agree with you on the point that we
disorganize the said club so that we may get your co-operation,
for our Union is operating under the instructions of the Central
Kuomintang with the object to protect the interests of our fellow
workmen. In order to avoid any unnecessary disputes or trouble
in the future, we advise you to keep a watchful eye on your Mr. Ma
and give him instruction to dissolve his club. In the meantime, we
shall pay special attention to steps taken by the "Tung Yih Club"
so that it will co-operate with you for mutual benefit.

Yours faithfully,
Chinese Seamen's Union.

(Sgd.) Yang Hu.

Special Commissioner.
page_data.zh:
中国海员工会杨虎致怡和洋行有限公司（Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd.）函副本
----------

中国海员工会，
上海西门

1936年11月26日。

致怡和洋行有限公司：

尊敬的先生们：

关于贵方11月10日来信要求我们修改通告第四条一事，我们要指出，该通告的性质是警告我们的会员不要从事任何非法行为。这绝非对工人的压迫。

除了拥有船上最高权威的船长发出的命令外，船员没有必要服从其他官员的所有命令，因为毕竟，他们不是奴隶。

贵方对部分员工不满意，因此不赞成我们的通函。至于“同益俱乐部”（Tung Yih Club），它是由不同船只的大副部门员工组成的，旨在促进彼此间的友好关系。如果贵方对其有足够的信心，这可能有助于你们的业务。经过我们的调查，我们发现该俱乐部被视为一个危险组织，因为贵方的马姓大副和一个名叫李的流氓正试图通过各种方式破坏它，以便组建一个符合他们利益的组织。

贵方来信中提到，一个叫王新清（Wang Sin Ching，音译）的人带着一群流氓强迫雇用某些工人。由于王新清是“同益俱乐部”的负责任成员，同时也是一个非常诚实的人，我们无法相信他会做出这样的事情。

我们也很难同意贵方关于我们要解散该俱乐部以获得贵方合作的观点，因为我们的工会是在国民党中央的指导下运作的，目的是保护我们工友的利益。为了避免将来任何不必要的争端或麻烦，我们建议贵方密切关注马先生，并指示他解散他的俱乐部。同时，我们将特别注意“同益俱乐部”采取的步骤，使其能与贵方合作，实现互利。

此致，

敬礼

中国海员工会。

（签名）杨虎。

特派专员。

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from the Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.
to General Yang Hu, Chinese Seamen's Union, Nantao.
-----------------

Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.
Shanghai, November 10, 1936.

General Yang Hu,
Chinese Seamen's Union,
West Gate.
Nantao.

Dear Sir,

We much appreciate your decree to the members of your
Union and you may be sure that the rules you have drawn up are,
in principle, in accordance with the good conduct, management
and discipline of a ship for the benefit of our shippers,
consignees and the travelling public. These are the principles
we aim at, keeping in mind justice and fair play to our employees.
We would like, however, to call your attention to Article 4.

The Captain necessarily delegates his authority to
his subordinate Officers in the execution of details of the ship's
work in the different departments. These Officers are responsible
to him and the heads of departments are, in turn, responsible
to the Officers.

We would suggest, therefore, an amendment to your
decree, making this clear.

In connection with this decree, we wish to bring to
your notice the case of the tallymen and watchmen of s.s. "Paowa".

Recently the neglect of these men occasioned the loss
of cargo to the extent of over $300.00. The Compadore paid for
this loss but that in no way makes up for the unsatisfactory
service given to shippers and consignees. The Compadore has
long wished to make changes in his staff but has been unable to
do so under pressure from your Union. We would be glad if this
matter can be cleared up satisfactorily.

We also wish to call to your notice unwarranted
interference with ship's discipline and routine in the Saloon
Department by certain persons purporting to represent your
Union without any reference to ourselves.

The first case is that of s.s. "Pansang".

The Steward, under instructions from the Master who
had reported the case to us, proposed to change one of his staff
who was dirty, negligent and in every way unsatisfactory.

He made arrangements with your Union to take a Union
man in his place but when the time came to make the change he
was informed that he could not discharge the unsatisfactory
member and the ship sailed with this man still on board on
Wednesday, November 4. We would be glad of an explanation of
this affair and also an assurance that this change will take
place without trouble on the return of s.s. "Pansang" on the
13th instant.

The second case is that of the "Kungwo" on the
6th instant.
page_data.zh:
印度支那轮船公司致中国海员工会杨虎将军函副本，地址：南市。
-----------------

印度支那轮船公司
上海，1936年11月10日。

致：
中国海员工会
杨虎将军
西门。
南市。

尊敬的先生：

我们非常感谢您向工会会员颁布的法令，您可以确信，您制定的规则原则上符合船舶的良好行为、管理和纪律，有利于我们的托运人、收货人和旅行公众。这些是我们旨在坚持的原则，同时铭记对我方员工的正义和公平。然而，我们要提请贵方注意第四条。

在执行船舶各部门工作的细节时，船长必然将其权力下放给其下属官员。这些官员对船长负责，而各部门主管则依次对这些官员负责。

因此，我们建议对贵方法令进行修改，以明确这一点。

关于此法令，我们希望提请您注意“宝华”号（s.s. "Paowa"，音译）轮的理货员和看守人员的案例。

最近，这些人的疏忽导致货物损失超过300美元。买办（Compadore）赔偿了这一损失，但这完全无法弥补给托运人和收货人带来的不满意服务。买办长期以来一直希望更换其员工，但在贵工会的压力下未能做到。如果此事能得到令人满意的解决，我们将不胜感激。

我们还希望提请您注意，某些声称代表贵工会的人士，在未与我方商议的情况下，对头等舱部门的船舶纪律和日常运作进行了无理干涉。

第一个案例是“潘桑”号（s.s. "Pansang"，音译）轮。

大副根据已向我方报告此案的船长的指示，提议更换其一名员工，该员工肮脏、疏忽，各方面都令人不满。

他与贵工会安排由一名工会成员接替，但当进行更换时，他被告知不能解雇这名令人不满的成员，该船于11月4日星期三启航时，此人仍在船上。我们希望就此事件得到解释，并保证在“潘桑”号于本月13日返回时，此次更换将顺利进行，不再产生麻烦。

第二个案例是本月6日的“公和”号。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

It was reported to us that certain members of
your Union had instructed the Steward to appoint a certain
boy, (Wang Kun Fo), from the "B" Saloon to be personal
servant to the new Chief Officer in place of the late Chief
Officer's boy who left with him.

Apart from the fact that the boy named is by no
means satisfactory, having absented himself from his place
of duty on board for two trips as reported by the Captain,
we do not tolerate this interference. It is a recognised
custom that the Chief Officer may choose his own boy. This
however was resisted by a force of about thirty loafers led
by one, Wang Tsui Chen, a member of the Ewo Boy's Club.

We have telegraphed to s.s. "Kungwo" that these
boys are to revert to their former positions. It is ridiculous
to suppose that a topass can assume the duties of a Saloon
boy.

The Third case is that of s.s. "Pingwo".

Some months ago you will recollect that, by mutual
agreement, two boys of s.s. "Pingwo" who deserted their ship
were re-instated on your guarantee of good behaviour and a
public apology to the Captain.

It has now been reported by the Captain that these two
boys devote their time to irritating the Steward who is in
charge of their department, and acting in a highly insubordinate
way towards him.

The same remarks apply to the similar case of the
Saloon boy of s.s. "Paowo".

This is not in accordance with the guarantee of
your Representatives. It is noteworthy also that all three
of the ships involved in the original trouble we had are the
subject of our complaints. We trace all these incidents to
the influence of the lately formed Ewo Boys Club.

We regret that we have to make all these complaints
about the conduct of our employees, particularly the Domestic
Staff. In the past our relations were of the best and we have
an excellent name for good service with our clients. Since,
however, the formation of this Ewo Boy's Club there has been a
series of troublesome incidents gravely affecting the
efficiency of our service.

In your letter of the 4th instant, covering your
decree, you ask for our co-operation. It is obvious that
co-operation is a reciprocal term so that, if you expect
co-operation from us, we must ask you to do your part in the
suppression of the activities of this Club.

It appears that this Club is acting in direct
contravention of our friendly relations and is doing its
best to stir up discontent and bad feeling among our employees.

We trust you will treat the contents of this letter
as urgent and important and take the necessary action.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,

General Managers. Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

据报，贵工会某些成员已指示管事任命一名来自“B”等舱（"B" Saloon）的特定男童（Wang Kun Fo，音译：王坤福/王昆福），担任新任大副的私人侍童，以接替随前任大副离职的侍童。

除了该指名男童远非令人满意这一事实外——正如船长所报告，他已在船上执勤期间两次擅离职守——我们也不容忍这种干涉。按照公认的习惯，大副有权选择自己的侍童。然而，这一权利遭到了一群约三十名无业游民的抵制，其头目为怡和侍童俱乐部（Ewo Boy's Club）成员 Wang Tsui Chen（音译：王粹臣/王翠珍）。

我们已电告“公和”轮（s.s. "Kungwo"），这些男童须恢复其原有职位。认为一名通事（topass）可以承担头等舱侍童（Saloon boy）的职责，这是荒谬的。

第三个案例涉及“平和”轮（s.s. "Pingwo"）。

几个月前，想必贵方还记得，经双方协议，“平和”轮两名弃船潜逃的男童在贵方担保其行为良好并向船长公开道歉后，得以复职。

现据船长报告，这两名男童将时间用于激怒负责管理他们的主管管事，并对他表现出极度的不服从行为。

同样的评论也适用于“宝和”轮（s.s. "Paowo"）头等舱侍童的类似案例。

这不符合贵方代表所作的担保。值得注意的是，最初引发我们麻烦的三艘船舶，如今都成为了我们投诉的对象。我们将所有这些事件归咎于最近成立的怡和侍童俱乐部的影响。

对于不得不就我们要员工，特别是家务职员的行为提出这些投诉，我们深表遗憾。过去，我们的关系最为融洽，我们在客户中享有服务优良的美誉。然而，自从该怡和侍童俱乐部成立以来，发生了一系列麻烦事件，严重影响了我们服务的效率。

在贵方本月4日来信中，附上了贵方的法令，并请求我们的合作。显然，“合作”是一个相互的术语，因此，如果贵方期望得到我们的合作，我们必须要求贵方尽其职责，压制该俱乐部的活动。

看来，该俱乐部的行为直接违背了我们的友好关系，并正竭力在我们的员工中煽动不满和不良情绪。

我们相信贵方会将本信内容视为紧急且重要事项，并采取必要行动。

此致
敬礼

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理

Copy of letter from General Yang Hu to Jardine Matheson
and Company, Ltd.
------------------

Chinese Seamen's Union,
Nantao, Shanghai.

November 4, 1936.

Shipping Department,
Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.
Shanghai.

Dear Sirs,

In company with this letter, we are sending you a
Decree recently issued by our Union to all our Union's members
calling their attention to certain particulars in regard to the
performance of their duties on board ships.

As our Union's members are scattering over different
ships, it is difficult to supervise the behaviour of each
individual member. We are therefore framing up certain rules,
as listed in our Decree, governing the behaviour of each of
our Union's members on board ships.

In the hope that our Decree will be strictly observed
by all our Union's members, we ask for your generous co-operation
with us. Should there be any misbehaviour on the part of our
Union's members, please advise us and we will enforce our
punishment accordingly.

Yours faithfully,

(chopped) Yang Hu.

杨虎将军致怡和洋行有限公司信函副本
------------------

中国海员工会，
上海南市。

1936年11月4日。

航运部，
怡和洋行有限公司，
上海。

敬启者：

随函附上本工会近期向所有会员发布的法令一份，提请他们注意关于在船上履行职责的某些具体事项。

由于本工会会员分散在不同的船只上，难以监督每个会员的行为。因此，我们制定了如法令中所列的若干规则，以规范本工会每位会员在船上的行为。

希望本工会所有会员严格遵守本法令，为此恳请贵方给予慷慨合作。若本工会会员有任何不当行为，请通知我们，我们将据此执行处罚。

此致
敬礼

（盖章）杨虎

page_data.en:
COPY

An outline of the Rules, as listed in the Chinese
Seamen's Union Decree, Governing the Behavior of
Union's Members on board ships

1. No union's members are allowed to smoke opium.
2. Union's members shall not smuggle or carry contraband goods.
3. Union's members must not ill-treat or insult passengers
and force passengers in regard to tipping.
4. Union's members must obey the Captain's or Purser's
order.
5. In case the ship is in peril, every Union's member must
exert his utmost to save the ship.
6. Union's members should not commit any action contrary to
the Regulations set up by the Union.
page_data.zh:
副本

中国海员工会法令中所列、规范工会会员在船上行为的规则概要

1. 工会会员不得吸食鸦片。
2. 工会会员不得走私或携带违禁品。
3. 工会会员不得虐待或侮辱乘客，不得强迫乘客给小费。
4. 工会会员必须服从船长或事务长的命令。
5. 若船舶遇险，每位工会会员必须竭尽全力救助船舶。
6. 工会会员不得从事任何违反工会制定规章的行为。

page_data.en:
Copy of letter from General Yang Hu to Jardine, Matheson
& Company, Ltd.

Chinese Seamen's Union,
Nantao, Shanghai.
October 8, 1936.

Shipping Department,
Jardine Matheson & Co. Ltd
Shanghai.

Dear Sirs,

We have received your letter of September 14 with
enclosed Regulations (English and Chinese attached).

In regard to these Regulations that you have framed
up for the guidance of your Saloon Staff, we have certain
comments to make.

As to Article 1 of the proposed regulations, we
entirely agree with what it now stands.

Article 2 relates to physical examination. We would
suggest that the examination should be taken once instead of
twice every year. If staff members are found to be unfit for
work, they should be sent to hospital. After their recovery,
they should be admitted to resume their respective work.

Respecting Article 3, we like to suggest that you
would revise this Article so as to permit only our Union's
unemployed members to fill in any vacancy which might appear
in the steward department.

We are also in accord with the provision in the
Article 4 of your proposed Regulations. However, we like to
suggest that promotion should be confined to our Union members.

As to Article 5, we propose that before punishing
any staff member, our Union must be notified.

Article 6 relates to absences or leaves of staff.
We suggest that members of staff should be entitled to ask
for leave thrice a year. The duration of leaves would of
course vary with needs on the part of staff.

We would entirely agree with the provision of
Article 7 relating to the wearing of uniform.

Respecting Article 8, we are of the opinion that
since you have set up definite working hours for your staff,
there is no need to keep record of their works.

Other than all articles which you have framed as
commented above, we would like to call your attention to add
one more article to your proposed regulations. This is to
grant the staff members, when oppressed by the Steward a right
to report to the steamer's Master directly, so that arrangement
may be made with our Union for investigation or settlement.

Hoping our suggestions will receive your favourable
consideration,

We are, dear Sirs,
Yours faithfully,

(chopped) Yang Hu
page_data.zh:
杨虎将军致怡和洋行有限公司信函副本

中国海员工会，
上海南市。
1936年10月8日。

航运部，
怡和洋行有限公司，
上海。

敬启者：

我方已收到贵方9月14日来信及所附规章（中英文附件）。

关于贵方为指导头等舱职员而制定的这些规章，我方有以下意见。

关于拟议规章的第一条，我方完全同意其现有内容。

第二条涉及体检。我方建议体检应每年进行一次，而非两次。若发现职员不适合工作，应送其就医。康复后，应准许其恢复各自的工作。

关于第三条，我方建议贵方修订此条，仅允许本工会的失业会员填补管事部门出现的任何空缺。

我方也同意贵方拟议规章第四条的规定。然而，我方建议晋升应仅限于本工会会员。

关于第五条，我方提议在处罚任何职员之前，必须通知本工会。

第六条涉及职员的缺勤或休假。我方建议职员应有权每年请假三次。假期长短自然视职员需求而定。

我方完全同意第七条关于穿着制服的规定。

关于第八条，我方认为，既然贵方已为职员规定了明确的工作时间，便无需记录他们的工作情况。

除上述已评论的各条款外，我方提请注意，建议在贵方拟议的规章中增加一条款。即赋予职员在受到管事压迫时，有权直接向轮船船长报告，以便与本工会安排调查或解决事宜。

希望我方建议能得到贵方的有利考虑，

此致
敬礼

（盖章）杨虎

General Yang Hu,
Chinese Seamen's Union,

Dear Sir,

Saloon Staff - Indo-China Steam Navigation Co. Ltd

Much time and patience has latterly been expended
on lengthy conferences on various matters arising out of the

印度支那轮船公司致南市中国海员工会信函副本

印度支那轮船公司
上海，1936年9月14日。

杨虎将军，
中国海员工会，
西门，
南市。

敬启者：

头等舱职员 - 印度支那轮船有限公司

近期，我们就头等舱职员行为引发的各种事项进行了长时间的会议，耗费了大量时间和耐心。

为了将来能有清晰的理解，我们制定了随附的规章（附中文译文）以指导我们的职员，并提议将其以中英文形式张贴在我们船只的公告板上。

我们认为贵方会同意这些规章对各方都是合理且公平的，如蒙贵方早日回复表示同意，我们将不胜感激。

此致
敬礼

印度支那轮船有限公司总经理

page_data.en:
COPY
REGULATIONS FOR SALOON STAFF

1. Discipline
Every person employed by the Company must be at all times
diligent in their respective duties and obedient to the lawful
commands of the Master and the General Managers. The Chief
Steward, as head of his Department, is responsible through
the Purser to the Master for the good order, discipline and
efficiency of his staff. Therefore, there must be close
co-operation between the Chief Steward and his staff to promote
good service and consequent benefit to all concerned.

2. Medical Examination
In accordance with the Principles of the New Life Movement
it is desirable that all employees, especially in this
particular branch of Service, should be clean and free from
disease. Therefore a medical examination of all the domestic
staff will take place at intervals of six months by
arrangement with the Government Quarantine Service. Men
suffering from incurable diseases will be discharged.

3. Engagement
As most of the Company's vessels are over-staffed with regular
employees and extra assistants who are not authorised, no
further staff will be engaged, except in emergency, until the
present unauthorised employees are absorbed. From that time
apprentices will be engaged as assistant pantry boys and
assistant cook-boys to learn the duties of the higher grades.
They will be required to register, with photograph, on the
Company's form.

4. Promotion
A roster is kept by all employees based on the Company's
form of registry which must be filled up by all employees.
Promotion will be made on length of service combined with
reports by the Master of efficiency and general behaviour.
page_data.zh:
副本
头等舱职员规章

1. 纪律
公司雇佣的所有人员必须时刻勤勉履行各自职责，并服从船长和总经理的合法命令。首席管事作为其部门主管，通过事务长向船长负责其下属的良好秩序、纪律和效率。因此，首席管事与其下属之间必须密切合作，以促进优质服务，从而使所有相关方受益。

2. 体检
根据新生活运动的原则，所有雇员，尤其是这一特定服务部门的雇员，应当保持清洁并无疾病。因此，所有家务职员将每隔六个月，通过与政府检疫服务部门安排，进行一次体检。患有不治之症者将被解雇。

3. 聘用
由于公司大多数船只的正式雇员和未经授权的额外助手人员过剩，在目前未经授权的雇员被吸收之前，除紧急情况外，不再聘用更多职员。从那时起，将聘用学徒作为助理餐具室男童和助理厨童，以学习更高阶层的职责。他们需在公司表格上登记并附照片。

4. 晋升
所有雇员均有一份基于公司注册表格的名单，所有雇员必须填写。晋升将结合服务年限以及船长关于效率和一般行为的报告进行。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

In view of the Chief Steward's large financial respon-
sibility, the position of Chief Cook and Pantry Boy store-
keeper will be filled by men who are acceptable to him.

5. Punishments for misbehaviour
Complaints of domestic staff will be investigated by the
Purser who will report the matter to the Master. He, in
turn, will render his report to the Company for the
necessary action to be taken. Serious offences such as
insubordination will be punished by dismissal.

6. Leave
All members of the staff are entitled to one trip off per
six months provided they can be spared. Requests for a
trip off must be forwarded through the Chief Steward and
Purser to the Master and should, if possible, be made
during the slack passenger season, viz. the Winter.

7. Uniform
The Company will provide uniforms for the domestic staff
and thereafter all members of the staff will be expected
to be well dressed when on duty.

8. Duty Book
A Duty Book will be kept by the Chief Steward detailing
boys for duty at times of the day other than meal times.
At meal times all the staff must be on duty.

September 14, 1936.
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

鉴于首席管事负有重大的财务责任，主厨和餐具室男童保管员的职位将由他所认可的人员担任。

5. 不当行为的处罚
对家务职员的投诉将由事务长调查，并由其向船长报告此事。随后，船长将向公司提交报告，以便采取必要行动。严重违纪行为，如不服从命令，将受到解雇处罚。

6. 休假
所有职员均有权每六个月享受一次免职航行（trip off），前提是人员调配允许。免职航行的请求必须通过首席管事和事务长转呈船长，并应尽可能在客运淡季，即冬季提出。

7. 制服
公司将为民务职员提供制服，此后所有职员在执勤时均须衣着整洁。

8. 值班簿
首席管事将保存一份值班簿，详细记录除用餐时间外各时段的值班男童。在用餐时间，所有职员必须在岗。

1936年9月14日。
上海。

Account regarding the wrong arrest of six Saloon
Staffs S.S. "Ping Wo", and Mr. Wilson Li 11th p.m.

Yesterday afternoon at about three o'clock, the six Saloon
Staffs together with Mr. Wilson Li, representative of the
Stewards Associated Office, were arrested by the armed
Chinese Police to the Garrison Headquarters at Lunghwa, (?)
and they were retained there until at present.

The information so far obtained is that on the 8th p.m. the
Investigating Officer from the Branch Union came on board
the "Pingwo" asking the six saloon staffs why they should
resign "Dong Yih Zoo" and they were required to go to the
Branch Union to give reasons. Thinking that the Union's
request should be obeyed, the Chief Stewards of "Pingwo"
& "Kungwo", Mr. Wilson Li, and 6 Saloon staffs went there
on the 9th p.m. to the Branch Union where the anti-Dong Yin Zoo
boys argued with the Dong Yih Zoo's boys. Their discussion
ended in failure. On the 10th, the Branch Union sent an official
letter to the "Pingwo" requesting again those anti-Dong
Yih Zoo boys to the Branch Union for explanation. On the
11th p.m., Mr. Wilson Li together with the six saloon
staffs went there as requested. When they reached there,
the Officers of the Seamen Union said to Mr. Wilson Li
that they wished to make a final adjustment with him.
Upon this the door was closed, and a heated discussion
followed, with noise indicating assault. Few minutes
later, the door was opened and immediately after armed
Chinese police entered, arrested all these men and hand-
cuffed two of them.

From the above statement, the matter is very clear that
as the Branch Union have always cooperated with the Dong
Yih Zoo for financial advantage the above seizure of lawful
persons has been well planned and arranged through all means.
Their aim is to intimidate Mr. Wilson Li to give up in the
first place, and to threaten the boys to stick to Dong Yih
Zoo to continue and increase their bad behaviour throughout
the Company's steamers. Mr. Wilson Li, and the anti-Dong
Yih Zoo boys have greatly been wronged, and it is earnestly
hoped that the Company should effect immediate release of
these men, and to make redress to this great grievance in
the future.

Shanghai, 12th March, 1937.
page_data.zh:
关于“平和”轮（S.S. "Ping Wo"）六名餐厅职员及Wilson Li先生被错误逮捕的情况说明，3月11日晚。

昨天下午三点左右，六名餐厅职员连同怡和洋行管事代表Wilson Li先生，被武装中国警察逮捕至龙华卫戍司令部，(?) 并被扣留至今。

目前获得的消息是，8日晚，分会工会的调查人员登上“平和”轮，询问六名餐厅职员为何要退出“同益社”，并要求他们去分会工会说明理由。认为应当服从工会的要求，“平和”轮和“公和”轮的大管事Wilson Li先生及六名餐厅职员于9日晚前往分会工会，在那里，反同益社的人员与同益社的人员发生了争执。他们的讨论以失败告终。10日，分会工会向“平和”轮发出正式信函，再次要求那些反同益社的人员到分会工会进行解释。11日晚，Wilson Li先生会同六名餐厅职员按要求前往。当他们到达那里时，海员工会的官员对Wilson Li先生说，希望与他做最后调解。随即大门关闭，随后发生了激烈的争论，嘈杂声表明发生了袭击。几分钟后，大门打开，武装中国警察立即进入，逮捕了所有人，并将其中两人戴上手铐。

从上述陈述来看，事情非常清楚，由于分会工会一直为了经济利益而同同益社合作，上述对守法人员的抓捕是经过精心策划和安排的。他们的目的是首先恐吓Wilson Li先生使其放弃，并威胁那些伙计坚持留在同益社，以便在公司所属轮船上继续并增加其恶劣行为。Wilson Li先生和反同益社的伙计们受到了极大的冤屈，恳切希望公司能促成这些人立即获释，并在未来对这一巨大冤屈予以补救。

上海，1937年3月12日。

Subject Arrest by Chinese Authorities of six employees of the Indo-China Steam
Navigation Company.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

At 6 p.m. March 11 information was received from
Commander Skyrme of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company
to the effect that during the afternoon six employees of his
company together with one Li Tai-zung (厲載臣) had been
arrested by the Chinese Authorities in Nantao. In explanation,
Commander Skyrme stated that on February 27, 1936, six saloon
boys of the s.s. "Pingwo," now in dry dock, resigned from the
Saloon Boys' Club. On March 11, it is stated, the six saloon
boys were requested by the Shanghai Branch of the Chung Hwa
Seamen's Union to attend at the offices of the Union in Nantao.
In company with Li Tai-zung representing the Ewo Stewards, the
six men went to the offices and were questioned by the Chief
of the Union as to their reasons for resigning from their club.
In the opinion of the Union representatives the saloon boys
failed to give satisfactory answers to their questions and it
appears that a dispute arose which resulted in the arrest of
both the saloon boys and Li Tai-zung.
The prisoners are now detained at the Woosung-Shanghai
Garrison Commander's Headquarters, Lunghwa.

Henchman
D. P. S.
