Subject Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - Unrest among
cooks of the s.s. "Kiawo" and s.s. "Kungwo"

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by T boyu D S I

Sz Ning-hwa (施紅華), the steward of the
s.s. "Kiawo" and Sz Teh-yoong (施德荣) of the
s.s. "Kungwo" of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company
are reported to have arranged between themselves to change
ships and both intend to take away with them three cooks
from each vessel. With the support of the saloon boys
of the two steamers, the cooks concerned are opposing to
this arrangement, and are negotiating with the stewards
for a settlement.

There are three cooks on the s.s. "Kiawo" and six
on the s.s. "Kungwo," the former being paid $38.00 and the
latter $18.00 per mensem. It is learned that the cooks on
the s.s. "Kungwo" obtain a large amount in tips from
passengers, although they receive lower wages. On the
contrary, the cooks on the s.s. "Kiawo" receive higher pay
but less in tips. The difference is due to the fact that
the s.s. "Kungwo" which runs between Hankow and Shanghai,
continues in service throughout the year, while the s.s.
"Kiawo," which runs between Chungking and Shanghai, suspends
at certain periods owing to low water.

Date February 17, 1937.
Subject S.S. "Kungwo" - Trouble anticipated between tallymen
and sailors
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J Boyne D S I
Information has been received from Commander
Skyrme of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company to the
effect that there is a possibility of trouble arising
between the tallymen and sailors of the s.s. "Kungwo" when
that vessel berths at Hunt's Wharf (Hongkew District) in the
forenoon of tomorrow, February 18.
Commander Skyrme stated that the cause of the
trouble concerned certain perquisites to which the sailors
were justly entitled. Before the "Kungwo" left Shanghai on
her present trip, the tallymen attempted to usurp the
privilege which the sailors claim as their right, to collect
and sell rice sweepings from the hold of the ship; the
sailors resisted, with the result that four tallymen were
injured and were left in Shanghai. After the ship had
left Hankow and was on its return voyage, the Captain was
informed that trouble was likely to occur when they docked
at Shanghai; he transmitted this information to his Company.
Commander Skyrme, however, has received information
subsequent to the foregoing that Wilson Li (勵國光), a
steward of the Company and Pang Pah-wei (彭伯威),
Chairman of the Seamen's Branch Union have settled the
dispute between the two parties and that trouble will not
occur. Commander Skyrme, though trusting Wilson Li, is
inclined to believe that in spite of this settlement, trouble
may occur, and he therefore requests that Police protection
be provided.

已从印度支那轮船公司的 Skyrme 指挥官处收到消息，称明日（2月18日）上午“公和”轮停靠亨特码头（虹口区）时，该轮理货员与水手之间有可能发生冲突。
Skyrme 指挥官称，冲突起因涉及水手正当享有的某些额外收益。在“公和”轮本次离沪前，理货员试图篡夺水手声称是其权利的收集并出售船舱内扫集稻米的特权；水手予以抵抗，导致四名理货员受伤并留在上海。该船离开汉口返程后，船长获悉在上海靠岸时可能会发生麻烦；他将此信息通报给公司。
然而，Skyrme 指挥官在此后收到消息，称该公司大副 Wilson Li（勵國光）与海员工会分会主席 Pang Pah-wei（彭伯威）已解决双方纠纷，不会发生骚乱。Skyrme 指挥官虽然信任 Wilson Li，但仍倾向于认为尽管已有此和解，骚乱仍可能发生，因此请求提供警察保护。

Subject Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - dispute between compradore
and tallymen of the s.s. "Prominent".

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I.

The s.s. "Prominent" arrived at Shanghai from the South
at 9 a.m. February 13, 1937 and tied up at No.2 Buoy in
midstream in order to avoid the possibility of trouble occur-
ring with the old tallymen. It will be recalled that the latter,
some 20 in number, during the last voyage of the "Prominent"
were involved in a fracas with an equal number of new hands
and were subsequently sent back to Shanghai.

At 1 p.m. February 13, Chen Ping Zung (郑聘臣), compradore
of the s.s. "Prominent", Bang Pah Wei (彭百威), and Wong Chi Ih
(王奇一) of the Seamen's Union, Chen Yuan Loong (陈元龙),
committee member of the Ewo Tallymen's Club, and Zung Tse Liang
(郑子良), a committee-man of the Chowchow Fellow Countrymen's
Association, met in the Shanghai Branch of the Chung Hwa Seamen's
Union, City, and eventually arrived at the following agreement:-

1. That the old tallymen resume work at 9 a.m. February 14, 1937.
2. That Assistant Compradore Mang Hou Foh (孟候福) be dismissed
from his employment (This person is alleged to have been
responsible for the assault on the old tallymen.)
3. That the five cabin boys who were involved in the fracas be
permitted to resume work.
4. That both sides issue instructions prohibiting the recur-
rence of trouble in the future.
5. That the hospital bills of the injured tallymen and the
new hands be paid by the Tallymen's Club and the compradore
respectively.
6. That the wages of the tallymen commencing from the date they
resume work be reduced by 10%. No wages are to be paid
for the period during which they did not work.

事由：印度支那轮船公司——“普罗米南特”轮买办与理货员之间的纠纷。

制作人：副督察长 Henchman 转呈人：J. Boyne 助理总监。

“普罗米南特”轮于1937年2月13日上午9时从南方抵达上海，为避免与原有理货员发生麻烦，系泊于江心的2号浮筒。需回顾的是，在上一次“普罗米南特”轮航行期间，约20名原有理货员与同等数量的新手发生斗殴，随后被送回上海。

1937年2月13日下午1时，“普罗米南特”轮买办郑聘臣（Chen Ping Zung）、海员工会的彭百威（Bang Pah Wei）和王奇一（Wong Chi Ih）、怡和理货员俱乐部委员陈元龙（Chen Yuan Loong）以及潮州同乡会委员郑子良（Zung Tse Liang）在位于市区的中华海员工会上海分会会面，并最终达成如下协议：-

1. 原有理货员于1937年2月14日上午9时复工。

At about 2 p.m. February 6, 1937, four persons claiming
to represent those tallymen of the s.s. "Prominent" who had
been sent back to Shanghai in consequence of a fight which
occurred on board the vessel on February 4 (Vide report dated
6/2/37), called at the Chung Hwa Seamen's Union, No.33 Oong
Ka Loong, City, and requested the latter to submit the following
demands to the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company:-
1. That the Company should divulge the names of those new hands
who were responsible for the assault on the old tallymen.
2. That the compradores of the vessel be dealt with adequately.
3. That the Company pay the hospital bills of the injured tally-
men and grant a certain sum to their families for their
maintenance.
4. That the Company should provide maintenance for the old
tallymen while they are not working.
5. That the Company should notify the Seamen's Union when a
a change of staff employed on vessels is contemplated.

persons the following six reside in Rooms No.21 and No.42 of

呈报人：D.P.S. Henchman 转呈人：J. Logan D.S.I

1937年2月6日下午2时许，四名自称代表“Prominent”号轮理货员的人士前往位于市区翁家弄33号的中华海员工会，这些理货员是因2月4日在该船上发生斗殴事件而被遣返回上海的（参见1937年2月6日的报告），他们请求工会向印度支那轮船公司提出以下要求：
1. 公司应揭露那些对老理货员实施袭击的新手姓名。
2. 对该船的买办予以适当处理。
3. 公司应支付受伤理货员的医院账单，并向其家属提供一定数额的赡养费。
4. 公司在老理货员失业期间应为其提供生活维持费。
5. 当公司计划变更船上雇员时，应通知海员工会。
工会部门主任王雅倫（Wong Yah Lung）承诺将认真考虑他们的请求，得到这一保证后，代表团离去。
2月6日，此前于2月5日曾前往莱斯华人医院（Chinese Lester Hospital）就诊的四名受伤理货员，又前往霞飞路的永全医院（Yung Chuen Hospital）；陪同他们的还有四名同事，据称这些同事也在斗殴中受伤。接受治疗后，医院为每人出具了证明并准予出院。在这八人中，以下六人居住在西华德路568弄2号西华德寄宿舍的21号和42号房间：
1. 朱天飛（Tsu Tien Faa）

REPORT
Date. February 6, 1937.

Subject Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - fracas between the old
tallymen and new hands aboard the s.s. "Prominent".
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne. D.S.S.

At 8 p.m. February 4, 1937, when the s.s. "Prominent"
of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Co., was already some
distance outside Woosung, a dispute concerning accommodation,
occurred. This dispute resulted in a fracas between some
20 of the old tallymen and an equal number of those tallymen
who were being repatriated to Hongkong. Four of the old
tallymen were injured and were subsequently taken to hospital.
The ship returned to Woosung and the Captain arranged
with the Water Police for the latter to escort both the old
tallymen and those who were to have been repatriated, back
to Shanghai. The ship subsequently resumed her voyage for
the South.
On arrival at the Customs Jetty the old tallymen
returned to the Seward Lodging House, Lane 568 No.2 East
Seward Road, while the remainder dispersed. The four
injured tallymen afterwards attended the Chinese Lester
Hospital but were discharged after having received treatment.
It is reported that Zao Ling (赵霖), a lawyer engaged
by the Ewo Tallymen's Club will bring the injured tallymen
before the Shanghai District Court to-day for examination
and that the Club in question will submit demands to the
Indo-China Navigation Company for the dismissal of Zung
Ping Zung (郑鹏程), the comprador of the s.s. "Prominent",
and the payment of the hospital bills of the injured tallymen.
It is the intention of the Indo-China Steam Navigation
Company to repatriate the Hongkong tallymen as soon as possible.

主题：印度支那轮船公司——“Prominent”号轮上老理货员与新手之间的斗殴。
呈报人：D.P.S. Henchman 转呈人：J. Boyne. D.S.S.

1937年2月4日晚8时，印度支那轮船公司的“Prominent”号轮已驶离吴淞一段距离，此时因住宿问题发生争执。这场争执导致约20名老理货员与同等数量的被遣返香港的新理货员之间发生斗殴。四名老理货员受伤，随后被送往医院。
该船返回吴淞，船长与水警队安排，由水警队护送老理货员及原定被遣返者返回上海。随后该船继续向南航行。
抵达海关码头后，老理货员返回位于东西华德路568弄2号的西华德寄宿舍，其余人员则四散离开。四名受伤的理货员事后前往莱斯华人医院就诊，接受治疗后被准予出院。
据报道，怡和理货员俱乐部聘请的律师赵霖（Zao Ling）将于今日将受伤理货员带至上海地方法院接受讯问，且该俱乐部将向印度支那轮船公司提出要求，解雇“Prominent”号轮买办郑鹏程（Zung Ping Zung），并支付受伤理货员的医院账单。
印度支那轮船公司打算尽快将这些香港理货员遣返。

THE CHINA PRESS SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 1937

Crew Fight
Causes Ship
To Return

Norwegian Freighter
Puts 4 Ashore After
Knife Battle

UNION TROUBLE IS
BELIEVED CAUSE

S.S. Prominent Captain
Orders Vessel Back
To Woosung

A fight on the high seas between members of the Chinese crew of the s.s. Prominent, Norwegian freighter now under charter to Jardine Matheson and Company, Ltd., forced that vessel to return to Shanghai yesterday morning for purpose of putting four men in need of medical treatment ashore.

The fight occurred early yesterday morning in the quarters of the Chinese crew. Knives flashed and four men were wounded, one of whom was rather badly cut up about the face and neck. The other sustained only minor wounds but were in need of more medical attention than mere first aid, which was all that could be given aboard the ship.

The battle started, a CHINA PRESS reporter learned last night, as the result of an argument which had developed between union men and a few non-union hands who happened to be on the boat. The union men apparently believed that the non-union seamen had no right to be on the vessel and after lengthy verbal fireworks, the argument developed into a pitched battle in which knives were the principal weapons.

Learning of the trouble, the ship's officers proceeded to the crew's quarters and succeeding in stopping the fracas and restoring order. The four principals of the dispute, it was found, also were wounded and rather than keep them on board until he reached Hongkong, the destination of the ship, the captain decided to turn back and hand the men over to the Customs authorities at Woosung for transfer to the River Police.

The ship was turned about at once and reached Woosung shortly before noon yesterday. The men were placed aboard a Customs launch and reached the Customs Jetty on the Bund about 3 p.m. They were taken by ambulance to the Lester Chinese Hospital where their wounds were treated and were then handed over to the Central Police Station where they were kept for a few hours before being turned over to the River Police. It is understood that they will be placed in the hands of the Special District Court in Nantao for trial.

In the meantime the s.s. Prominent has left Woosung and is again back on her way to Hongkong, having lost practically a day because of the fight.

The Prominent is a vessel of about 4,000 tons gross tonnage, Norwegian built, and has been in China waters for some time. She recently was chartered by Jardine Matheson & Co. for operation along the

《大美晚报》 1937年2月6日，星期六

船员斗殴
致船只
返航

挪威货轮
刀战后遣四人上岸

相信工会纠纷
是起因

“Prominent”号轮船长
命令船只返回
吴淞

目前由怡和洋行有限公司承租的挪威货轮“Prominent”号轮的中国船员在公海上发生斗殴，迫使该船于昨晨返回上海，以便将四名需要医疗救治的人员送上岸。

斗殴发生于昨日清晨中国船员的居住区。刀具挥舞，四人受伤，其中一人面部和颈部受创较重。其他人仅受轻伤，但需要的医疗护理超出了简单的急救，而船上只能提供急救。

据《大美晚报》记者昨晚获悉，这场争斗起因于工会成员与船上几名非工会工人之间发生的争吵。工会成员显然认为非工会海员无权留在船上，经过长时间的口角后，争吵升级为持刀混战。

得知骚乱后，船方官员前往船员居住区，成功制止了斗殴并恢复了秩序。经查，纠纷中的四名主要当事人也受了伤，船长决定不再让他们随船前往目的地香港，而是折返，在吴淞将这些人移交给海关当局，再转交水警队。

船只立即掉头，于昨日中午前不久抵达吴淞。这些人被送上一艘海关快艇，并于下午3点左右抵达外滩的海关码头。他们由救护车送往莱斯华人医院治疗伤口，随后被移交至中央捕房，在那里扣留数小时后移交给水警队。据悉，他们将被移送至南市特区法院受审。

与此同时，“Prominent”号轮已离开吴淞，重新踏上前往香港的旅程，因这次斗殴几乎耽误了一天时间。

“Prominent”号轮是一艘总吨位约4,000吨的挪威建造船只，已在中国水域航行一段时间。最近由怡和洋行有限公司承租，用于沿……运营

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 1937

Crew Fights:
Steamer Puts
Back to Port

Injured Chinese Landed at
Customs Jetty

FRACAS AMONG TEA-BOYS
IN S.S. PROMINENT

A fight which grew to such proportions that it became necessary to bring a ship back to port a few hours after sailing, was revealed when four injured Chinese were brought up-river from Woosung and loaded into an ambulance at the Customs Jetty yesterday afternoon. The ss. Prominent, a Norwegian vessel, sailed from Shanghai for Swatow on Thursday. Trouble developed between rival factions in the comprador's staff of tea-boys and spread until a large group of the ship's complement were feeling the effects. The master of the vessel eventually found it necessary to turn her around and put back to Woosung, where the River Police were called on to lend a hand.

A party left Shanghai at 9 a.m. for Woosung in a launch under the direction of Mr. W. C. Woodfield, Superintendent of the River Police. They included one of the Norwegian Vice-Consuls and a foreign doctor.

On their arrival, the master of the Prominent requested the police to remove about 30 of the more pugnacious members of the crew but preferred no charges against them. The four members of the crew who were most severely injured were brought back to Shanghai in the launch and sent to the Lester Chinese Hospital in a Fire Brigade ambulance.

Get Up and Walk

At the hospital, shortly after 2 p.m., two were treated for contusions of the chest, one for lacerations of the face, and the fourth for a bruise of the hip. They were then told to get up and walk which they did right out of the hospital.

The fracas on the ship was between union and non-union parties, under the leadership of rival compradores. The services of the old comprador and his men had been dispensed with previously, but they came to Shanghai and boarded the vessel shortly before she sailed. The difficulties between the old comprador and the new comprador were hastily patched up and the vessel sailed out of the harbour in a peaceful fashion on Thursday morning.

When she reached Woosung, the trouble broke out again between the two factions and the master found it necessary to call for police assistance.

The vessel is chartered by Jardine, Matheson & Company, Ltd.

船员斗殴：
轮船
折返港口

受伤华人在
海关码头登陆

“Prominent”号轮
茶房斗殴

一艘船在启航数小时后因斗殴规模扩大而被迫返港，这一事件随着昨日下午四名受伤华人从吴淞溯江而上并在海关码头被送上救护车而曝光。挪威船只“Prominent”号轮于周四从上海驶往汕头。买办属下的茶房中对立派系之间发生麻烦，并蔓延开来，直至船上大量人员受到影响。船长最终发现有必要调头返回吴淞，并召请水警队协助。

一支队伍于上午9时在河警总监 W. C. Woodfield 先生的指挥下乘快艇前往吴淞。成员包括一名挪威副领事和一名外籍医生。

抵达后，“Prominent”号轮船长请求警方带走约30名最具攻击性的船员，但未对他们提出指控。四名受伤最严重的船员被快艇带回上海，并由救火会救护车送往莱斯华人医院。

起身行走

下午2点后不久，在医院里，两人因胸部挫伤接受治疗，一人因面部撕裂伤接受治疗，第四人因臀部淤青接受治疗。随后他们被告知起身行走，他们便直接走出了医院。

船上的斗殴发生在工会和非工会两派之间，由对立的买办领导。老买办及其手下此前已被解雇，但他们在开船前不久来到上海并登上了该船。新老买办之间的困难得以匆忙修补，船只于周四早晨平静地驶离港口。

当船只抵达吴淞时，两派之间的麻烦再次爆发，船长发现有必要寻求警方援助。

该船由怡和洋行有限公司承租。

In connection with the opposition of the twenty-one tally-
men of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company's s.s. "Prominent"
to a decision of the new comprador of the vessel to dispense
with their services and to engage new hands in their stead .
(Vide I.R. 3/2/37), a meeting was held under the auspices of
the Shanghai Branch of the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour
Union, in the office of the Ewo Tallymen's Guild (怡和理貨俱樂部),
Lane 449, No.27 East Seward Road, at 12 noon February 3. The
following persons attended:-
· Zung Ping Zung (鄭聘臣), new comprador of the s.s.
"Prominent".
Ling Shao Liang (林祥良), Assistant comprador of the
s.s. "Prominent".
Zung Yuan Loong (陳元龍), standing committee member of the
Ewo Tallymen's Guild.
Zao Sz Ching (趙世鏡) of the Shanghai Branch of the Chung
Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union.
Yang Zeu Sung (楊瑞生) -do-
During the meeting, the new comprador agreed to cancel his
decision to dismiss the twenty-one tallymen, but he retained the
right to discharge with the approval of the Seamen's Union,
those who are found to be inefficient. He further promised to
repatriate the new hands who were engaged at Hongkong.
Commander Skyrme of Jardine, Matheson & Co., in a telephone
conversation stated that owing to the reversal of the comprador's
decision he was of the opinion that chances of trouble occurring
aboard this vessel had been considerably reduced.

鉴于印度支那轮船公司“Prominent”号轮的二十一名理货员反对该轮新买办作出的辞退他们并雇佣新人接替的决定（参见1937年2月3日情报报告），2月3日中午12时，在中华海员总工会上海分会的主持下，于东熙华德路27号449弄怡和理货俱乐部（Ewo Tallymen's Guild）办公室举行了一次会议。出席人员如下：
· 郑聘臣（Zung Ping Zung），“Prominent”号轮新买办。
林祥良（Ling Shao Liang），“Prominent”号轮副买办。
陈元龙（Zung Yuan Loong），怡和理货俱乐部常务委员。
赵世镜（Zao Sz Ching），中华海员总工会上海分会代表。
杨瑞生（Yang Zeu Sung）——同上——

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by I. Boyne O.S.I.

At 10 a.m. 3rd February, 1937, a telephone message was
received from Commander Skyrme of Jardine, Matheson and Co. Ltd.
to the effect that one Chen Yuan Lung (陈元龙) of the Ewo Tally-
men's Club, Seward Road, had in company with a number of Chinese
of the loafer class, forced his way aboard the s.s. "Prominent",
berthed at Hunt's Wharf in Hongkew District, and had threatened
to create a disturbance unless certain tallymen who had been
dismissed were reinstated.
Commander Skyrme went on to explain that when the s.s.
"Prominent", a vessel chartered by Jardine, Matheson and Co.,
reached Hongkong it was found necessary to discharge the
tallymen who had travelled with the ship from Shanghai.
A new set of non-union tallymen were engaged but the old
employees remained aboard and returned to Shanghai as passengers.
When the ship tied up at Hunt's Wharf on 3rd February these men
refused to go ashore and are still aboard. The s.s. "Prominent"
is due to sail at 4 p.m. tomorrow, 4th February, but trouble
may be expected when cargo is loaded this morning.

1937年2月3日上午10时，接到怡和洋行有限公司Skyrme指挥官的电话消息，称熙华德路怡和理货俱乐部的陈元龙（Chen Yuan Lung）伙同数名无业游民性质的华人，强行登上停泊在虹口区亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf）的“Prominent”号轮，并威胁说，除非复职某些被辞退的理货员，否则将制造骚乱。
Skyrme指挥官进一步解释说，当由怡和洋行包租的“Prominent”号轮抵达香港时，发现有必要辞退随船从上海前来的理货员。
于是雇佣了一批新的非工会理货员，但老雇员仍留在船上，作为乘客返回上海。2月3日该船靠泊亨特码头时，这些人拒绝上岸，至今仍留在船上。“Prominent”号轮定于明天2月4日下午4时开航，但预计今天上午装货时可能会发生麻烦。

Subject Activities of the Two River and Seagoing Steamer Saloon
Boys' Mutual Advantage Society, Lane 449, No.27 E/Seward Road
Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by J. Bayne D.S.I

Following an interview with Commander Skyrme
regarding the activities of the Two River and Seagoing
Steamer Saloon Boys' Mutual Advantage Society, it was
agreed that a warning from the Police might curtail the
activities of the Society. Accordingly, Wong Zoen-ching
(王震慶), representative of the society, was called to
the office of the Special Branch during the afternoon of
February 1, 1937. He was informed that the members of the
Society were accused of boarding the s.s. "Kutwo" at Hunts
Wharf on January 24, 1937 and using threats in an endeavour
to induce the cabin boys on the vessel to join the Society.
In reply, Wong Zoen-ching admitted that members of the
Society had visited the vessel but denied that any threats
had been used. He was then informed that these visits to
vessels were unauthorized and must be discontinued, otherwise
action would be taken against the promoters of the Society.
Wong Zoen-ching agreed to discontinue these visits and
promised that the company would experience no more difficulty
from the Society.

在与Skyrme指挥官就两江及远洋轮船茶房互助社的活动进行面谈后，双方一致认为警方的警告可能会遏制该社的活动。因此，该社代表王震慶（Wong Zoen-ching）于1937年2月1日下午被召至特务科办公室。警方告知他，该社成员被指控于1937年1月24日在亨特码头登上“Kutwo”号轮，并使用威胁手段试图诱使船上的茶房加入该社。
对此，王震慶承认该社成员曾访问过该船，但否认使用了任何威胁手段。随后警方告知他，这些登船访问是未经授权的，必须停止，否则将对发起该社的人采取行动。
王震慶同意停止此类访问，并承诺该公司不会再受到该社的困扰。

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Moore

At 10.30 a.m. January 24, the following six members
of the "Ewo River and Seagoing Steamer Saloon Boys' Mutual
Advantage Society", Lane 449, No.27 East Seward Road,
appeared on the s.s. "Kutwo" of the Indo-China Steam
Navigation Company, which was berthed at the Hunt's Wharf,
in an endeavour to induce the saloon boys on board to join
the Society :-

Wong Zoen-ching (王善慶)
Peo Dao-fah (包道發)
Tseu Wen-yien (周文賢), saloon boy of the s.s."Suiwo".
Yue Hwa-zieng (俞華祥), saloon boy of the s.s."Paowo".
Yang Chu-yoong (楊智熊), saloon boy of the s.s.
"Fausang".
Loh Wen-sung (陸文生), saloon boy of the s.s.
"Siangwo".

These persons were alleged to have threatened to bring about
the dismissal of the non-members from the vessel if they did
not join the Society within a period of one month.

The stewards of the vessel intervened, and advised
the visitors to refer any labour matter to the Chung Hwa
Seamen's General Labour Union, Nantao, whereupon an altercation
took place between the two parties, but the society members
later dispersed without conducting further agitation.

There are twenty-six saloon boys on board the s.s.
"Kutwo", 22 of whom have not yet become members of the
Mutual Advantage Society.

呈报人及转呈人：D.I. Moore

1月24日上午10时30分，以下六名“怡和两江及远洋轮船茶房互助社”（地址：东熙华德路27号449弄）成员出现在停泊于亨特码头的印度支那轮船公司“Kutwo”号轮上，试图诱使船上的茶房加入该社：

王善慶（Wong Zoen-ching）
包道發（Peo Dao-fah）
周文賢（Tseu Wen-yien），“Suiwo”号轮茶房。
俞華祥（Yue Hwa-zieng），“Paowo”号轮茶房。
楊智熊（Yang Chu-yoong），“Fausang”号轮茶房。
陸文生（Loh Wen-sung），“Siangwo”号轮茶房。

据称，这些人威胁说，如果非会员在一个月内不加入该社，将导致他们被辞退出船。

船上的管事介入其中，建议来访者将任何劳工事务提交至南市的中华海员总工会，随后双方发生了争执，但该社成员后来散去，未再进行进一步的煽动活动。

“Kutwo”号轮上有二十六名茶房，其中22人尚未成为互助社成员。

REPORT Date January 22, 1937
Subject Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - Dispute between
Saloon Boys and Stewards Settled
Made by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Moore

Saloon boys, numbering some 220 in all, of the
Indo-China Steam Navigation Company recently agitated
against ill-treatment by stewards, and requested the
Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union, 33 Oong Ka Tse
Loong, Nantao, to mediate in the dispute. The saloon boys
submitted the following demands to stewards for consideration:-
1. That no saloon boys be discharged without reason, and
that no personal followers of stewards be employed.
2. That stewards should not retain wages of saloon boys.
3. That stewards should not interfere with division of
tips granted to saloon boys by passengers.
4. That the system requiring successors to pay for cooking
utensils and provisions owned by stewards when the
latter resign be abolished.
To counteract the demands of the saloon boys, the
stewards put up the following terms :-
1. That stewards have the authority to engage or dismiss
saloon boys.
2. That stewards distribute the wages to saloon boys.
3. That stewards should participate in the division of
tips granted by passengers.
4. That successors should pay for cooking utensils and
provisions owned by stewards when the latter resign.
At 2 p.m. January 21, a meeting was convened under
the auspices of the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union
in its office, 33 Oong Ka Tse Loong, Nantao, and the
following terms were agreed upon :-
1. That in future, tips granted by passengers be equally
divided among stewards and saloon boys.

报告 日期：1937年1月22日
事由：印度支那轮船公司——茶房与管事之间的纠纷已解决
呈报人/及转呈人：D.I. Moore

印度支那轮船公司的茶房共计约220人，最近因遭受管事虐待而发起抗议，并请求位于南市翁家宅路33号的中华海员总工会调解此纠纷。茶房向管事提出了以下要求供考虑：
1. 不得无故辞退茶房，不得雇用管事的私人亲信。
2. 管事不得扣留茶房的工资。
3. 管事不得干涉乘客给予茶房的小费分配。
4. 废除要求继任者在管事辞职时购买其拥有的炊具和备品的制度。
为对抗茶房的要求，管事提出了以下条件：
1. 管事有权雇用或辞退茶房。
2. 由管事向茶房分发工资。
3. 管事应参与分配乘客给予的小费。
4. 继任者应在管事辞职时购买其拥有的炊具和备品。
1月21日下午2时，在中华海员总工会的主持下，在其南市翁家宅路33号的办公室召开会议，并达成以下协议：
1. 今后，乘客给予的小费由管事和茶房平均分配。

provided by the Shanghai Branch of the Chung Hwa Seamen's
General Labour Union. According to the Saloon Boys' Union,
the matter will be taken up with the Indo-China Steam

Subject Activities of Seamen's Organizations in connection

Navigation Company - steward assaulted.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Moore

At about 7.30 a.m. August 7, a steward named Tse
Too Doo ( ) of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.
s.s. "Hsin Chingwo" was assaulted aboard the ship which was
berthed at Pootung, by a dismissed saloon boy and several
other disgruntled members of the saloon boy fraternity.
The River Police were called and they arrested
the dismissed saloon boy and two others, the former being
eventually charged with assault and causing a breach of the
peace.
At 4 p.m. August 7, Lt. Commander Skyome, Indo-
China Steam Navigation Co., informed the Special Branch by
telephone that the assaulted steward was staying aboard the
ship in charge of an officer but requested that the Municipal
Police give attention to the home of the steward who resides
at House Je9, Lane 224, Tongshan Road, as there is a likeli-
hood of attempts being made to interfere with his family.

Moore
D. S. I.
Wayside informed.

Subject Activities of Seamen's Organizations in connection
with the Chinese Staff of the Indo-China Steam
Navigation Company.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Moore.

One named Yao Yung-chong (姚永昌) was appointed
No.1 Cook to the S.S. "Suiwo" by the Indo-China Steam
Navigation Co. to replace the previous No.1 Cook who had died.
On July 6, 1936, in possession of a letter from the Company,
he proceeded to the vessel to take up his appointment but was
prevented from doing so by one Dzung Yah-chen (鄭佑成),
Secretary of the "Two River and Seagoing Steamers Saloon
Employees' Mutual Advantage Union" (怡和江海輪餐房部員工同益會)
with the assistance of some 10 loafers and the No.2 Cook of
the "Suiwo". Dzung Yah-chen and the No.2 Cook stated that
the No.1 Cook vacancy should be filled by the No.2 Cook, also
the appointment should be made with the approval of the Union.
Dzung took the letter of the Company away from Yao Yung-chong
and forced him to leave the ship. The "Suiwo" left Shanghai
on the evening of July 6, without Yao Yung-chong on board.
On July 7, 1936, Yao Yung-chong accompanied by an
official of the Company reported the incident at Hongkew
Police Station. Dzung Yah-chen was communicated with and
attended at the Station where he admitted that he prevented
Yao assuming his position as No.1 Cook, and argued that
Yao's appointment was illegal and could not be tolerated
from the point of view of the Union.
On July 15, the "Suiwo" returned to Shanghai and
Yao Yung-chong made a second attempt to take up his appointment
but failed owing to the strong opposition of the No.2 Cook.
On the advice of the Company, Yao appealed to the Shanghai
Branch Office of the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union,
40 Fu Tsung Ka, Dah Ching Road, Nantao, where he was verbally
promised full support by Chen Yung-ming (陳永銘), Section

印度支那轮船公司任命名为姚永昌（Yao Yung-chong）者为“瑞和”号轮船（S.S. "Suiwo"）头厨，以接替此前去世的头厨。1936年7月6日，他持公司信函前往该船就职，但遭到“江海轮船餐房部员工同益会”（怡和江海輪餐房部員工同益會）秘书郑佑成（Dzung Yah-chen，注：此处原文拼音为Dzung Yah-chen，前文为Dzung Yah-chien，后文多作Dzung Yah-chen，依上下文及常见译名习惯，结合后文括号内中文名鄭佑成，统一译为郑佑成）以及约十名游民和“瑞和”号二厨的阻挠。郑佑成和二厨声称，头厨空缺应由二厨填补，且任命须经工会批准。郑从姚永昌手中夺走公司信函，并强迫其离船。“瑞和”号于7月6日晚离开上海，姚永昌未能登船。
1936年7月7日，姚永昌在公司一名官员陪同下，向虹口警署报案。警方与郑佑成取得联系，郑到警署承认阻止姚就任头厨一职，并辩称姚的任命非法，从工会立场来看不能容忍。
7月15日，“瑞和”号返回上海，姚永昌再次尝试就职，但因二厨的强烈反对而失败。在公司建议下，姚向南市大庆路福总街40号的中华海员总工会上海办事处求助，该办事处科长陈永銘（Chen Yung-ming）口头承诺给予全力支持，

Labour Union and is on very intimate terms with Pang Fah-wei

a favoured follower of General Yang Hu, Woosung-Shanghai

Dismissal of two saloon boys on the s.s. "Pingwo"
Two saloon boys named Huang Feng-do (王根度) and
Cheng Fok-sung (張福生), of the s.s. "Pingwo", berthed at
the Old Ningpo Wharf, left the vessel at 4 p.m. July 28
without permission of the Captain. On the morning of July
29, they were summoned back to the ship and instructed to
give an explanation for their absence, failing which they
would be dismissed. At 8.30 p.m. July 29, Chen Yuen-loong
(陳元龍), Chairman of the Ewo Steamship Tallymen's Club,
accompanied by one named Yang claiming to be a Secretary
of the Shanghai Branch Office of the Chung Hwa Seamen's
General Labour Union and five loafers boarded the "Pingwo",
and in the absence of the Chief Steward informed the 2nd
Steward that the two saloon boys could not be dismissed
without the approval of the Union and that the Chief Steward
would be held responsible for their employment. The two
saloon boys were eventually dismissed by the Captain and left
the ship at 10p.m. July 29. The "Pingwo" left Shanghai at
4.30 a.m. July 30 without any further trouble.
As far as can be ascertained, the other saloon boys
and the kitchen staff of this steamer have no desire to raise
any opposition to the dismissals unless the Union brings
pressure to bear on them. It is learned that the Ewo River

停泊在老宁波码头的“平和”号轮船的两名侍者，名为王根度（Huang Feng-do，注：拼音Huang对应黄，但中文标注为王，依中文标注译出）和张福生（Cheng Fok-sung，注：拼音Cheng对应程/郑，但中文标注为张，依中文标注译出），于7月28日下午4时未经船长许可擅自离船。7月29日上午，他们被召回船上，并被要求解释缺席原因，否则将被解雇。7月29日晚8时30分，怡和轮船理货员俱乐部主席陈元龍（Chen Yuen-loong）由一名自称中华海员总工会上海办事处秘书的杨姓男子及五名游民陪同，登上“平和”号，在总管事不在场的情况下告知二管事，未经工会批准不得解雇这两名侍者，否则总管事需对他们的雇佣负责。最终，这两名侍者被船长解雇，并于7月29日晚10时离船。“平和”号于7月30日凌晨4时30分离开上海，未发生进一步麻烦。

Subject Threatened trouble between the Compradore of the s.s. "Suiwo",
Jardine, Matheson & Co., and the Ewo Tallymen's Club.
Made by D.P.S. Mackay. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the telephone message received
by D.C. (Special Branch) on the morning of September 4, from
Jardine, Matheson & Co., I have to report investigation of the
attempt of the Ewo Tallymen's Club to force the Compradore of
the s.s. "Suiwo" to dismiss two of his tallymen.
These two tallymen are old members of the Comprad-
ore's staff, are not members of the Ewo Tallymen's Club, and in
a recent strike of tallymen of the s.s. "Suiwo" remained loyal
to the compradore and refused to strike. Consequently, attempts
were made by the Club to have these two men dismissed, and in
order to avoid trouble the two men attempted to join the Club.
Their applications, however, were refused, and the compradore
was requested by the Tallymen's club to suspend them from work.
This the compradore refused to do, and on August 21 received a
letter from the Chinese Seamen's Union requesting his to dismiss
the men, replacing them by club members. The compradore took
no action in the matter, and on August 26 the Ewo Tallymen's
Club appointed two members to replace the non-Club workers. The
newly appointed tallymen sailed with the boat, but the compradore
refused to allow them to work. On August 29 the compradore
received a letter of complaint from the Ewo Tallymen's Club, in
regard to his action in preventing the two new men from working,
and when the s.s. "Suiwo" docked on the morning of September 4
the Chairman of the Ewo Tallymen's Club was waiting to interview
the Compradore. Owing to the presence of Police in the vicinity,
no untoward occurrence took place.

No. 27 Seward Road, with Zung Yuan-loong (陳元龍) as

关于特别处主任（D.C. (Special Branch)）于9月4日上午收到怡和洋行的电话留言，兹报告对怡和理货员俱乐部试图强迫“绥和”轮买办解雇其两名理货员一事的调查结果。
这两名理货员是买办班底的老成员，并非怡和理货员俱乐部会员，且在近期“绥和”轮理货员罢工期间忠于买办，拒绝参加罢工。因此，该俱乐部试图解雇这两人，而为了避免麻烦，这两人曾试图加入该俱乐部。然而，他们的申请被拒，且理货员俱乐部要求买办停止这两人的工作。买办拒绝了这一要求，并于8月21日收到中国海员工会的来信，要求其解雇这些人，并由俱乐部成员取而代之。买办对此事未采取行动，8月26日，怡和理货员俱乐部指派了两名成员接替非俱乐部工人的职位。新指派的理货员随船出航，但买办拒绝让他们工作。8月29日，买办收到怡和理货员俱乐部的投诉信，指责他阻止两名新人工作；当“绥和”轮于9月4日上午靠岸时，怡和理货员俱乐部主席正等候会见买办。由于附近有警察在场，未发生任何意外事件。

E-WO RIVER AND COAST STEAMERS' TALLYMEN'S CLUB

Shanghai, 29 August, 1935.

The Compradore
S. S. "Suiwo"

Dear Sir,

Referring to our conversation in your house on
Saturday last, you had promised us then that you would give
us a reply on Monday at 3 p.m. However, we waited till
5 p.m. on that day, but there came no news from you. In
accordance with the instructions from the Seamen's Union,
two members were then sent to your ship to fill the vacancy.

At the time of your ship's departure, the writer
went on board again but you did not see him. Evidently, you
have treated us with contempt, and playing a trick as a child.

Now while the ship was on the voyage, you, on the
pleas that no settlement has been come to with the Club, pre-
vented our two men from going into the cargo holds to perform
their duties. Such action is quite wrong. Besides instructing
the two men to take up their duties in the cargo holds, we
write you this for your information. If you have any opinion
to express, we shall wait for you at the wharf on your return
to Shanghai.

Yours faithfully,
Chan Yuen Loong,
Executive Committee

怡和内河及沿海轮船理货员俱乐部

上海，1935年8月29日。

“绥和”轮买办
先生台鉴：

提及上周六在府上的谈话，当时您承诺将于周一下午3时给予答复。然而，我们等到当天下午5时，仍未收到您的消息。根据海员工会的指示，随后派遣两名会员前往贵船填补空缺。

在贵船离港时，本人再次登船，但您并未接见。显然，您对我们轻蔑相待，如同儿戏般耍弄手段。

现在，在船舶航行期间，您以尚未与俱乐部达成和解为由，阻止我方两人进入货舱履行职责。此举大错特错。除指令该两人进入货舱履职外，特致函告知。若您有任何意见，待您返回上海时，我们将在码头等候。

此致
敬礼
陈元龙，
执行委员会

page_data.en:
Compadore of s.s. "Suiwo"
August 28, 1935 (From Nanking)

The Manager,
J. L. & Co.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,
    I beg to inform you that as I have reported to Mr. Frost
twice about the Union pressed me to dismiss two of my stevadors
and replace their own members. These two stevadors are my own men,
work hard for many years, not join the Union, they did not stop
their work at the time when they strike (For s.s. 'Chip Sang's case,
two trips ago). By this reason they found out they were going on
their work without any stop, so they are angry with these two saying
they must replace two Union men instead of this two or they promise
to join the Union immediately.
    These two old men went to Union on Monday afternoon ask
for join the Union to be their members begin from to-day, because
they are afraid to loose their positions, or make any big trouble.
But they refused and says, you are not allowed to join our Union
because the time is too late. After that they really sent two men
to ship, stop these two old men to dinner (they came when they chow
together) with them and take away their baggages and replaced their
own members' baggages on the berths. These Union men are still on
board, I can only stop them going to the cargo hall, but I cannot
do any more to against them, because I am afraid to make any big
trouble so I write to report you and beg you will help me to settle
this then we can safely to do our work.
    I hand you all the Union letters sent me a few days. Begging
you will be kindly to help me to settle this with Union early, if not
they will make some more or bigger trouble with me when we back to
Shanghai. Thanking you very much.

                                I am,
                                    Dear Sir,
                                        Yours respectfully,
                                            Dung Pey
page_data.zh:
“绥和”轮买办
1935年8月28日（自南京）

经理，
怡和洋行（J. L. & Co.）
上海。

尊敬的先生：
    谨此告知，我曾两次向弗罗斯特先生（Mr. Frost）报告，工会迫使我解雇两名装卸工并替换为他们自己的人。这两名装卸工是我自己的人，多年来努力工作，未加入工会，在罢工期间（即前两次航次的“吉盛”轮 s.s. 'Chip Sang' 案例中）并未停工。正因如此，他们发现这两人继续工作而未停工，便对这两人感到愤怒，声称必须用两名工会成员替换这两人，否则他们承诺立即加入工会。
    这两名老工人于周一下午前往工会，申请从今天起成为工会会员，因为他们害怕失去职位或引发大麻烦。但工会拒绝并表示，你们不准加入我们的工会，因为时间太晚了。之后，他们确实派了两个人到船上，阻止这两名老工人吃饭（他们来时就在一起吃饭），并拿走了他们的行李，将工会成员的行李放在铺位上。这些工会人员仍在船上，我只能阻止他们进入货舱，但我无法采取更多措施对抗他们，因为我害怕引发大麻烦，故写信向您报告，恳请您帮助解决此事，以便我们能安全工作。
    现将几天前工会寄给我的所有信件呈上。恳请您 kindly 帮助我尽早与工会解决此事，否则当我们回到上海时，他们会给我制造更多或更大的麻烦。非常感谢。

                                此致，
                                    尊敬的先生，
                                        您忠实的，
                                            Dung Pey

s.s. "Suiwo"

Shanghai, August 21, 1935.

The Compradore,
S.S. "Suiwo,"

Dear Sir,

We have just received a petition from the
E-wo River and Coast Steamers Tallymen's Club stating that
on board the s.s. "Suiwo," there are three Watchmen, namely
Ta Fuh, Yao Kwei Fah and Shu Kwong Yu who are not members
of the Seamen's Union but are working in the cargo holds.
Moreover, they do not obey the directions of the Club
and are doing things which are detrimental to the good
reputation of the organization. The Union are therefore
requested to take up the matter and will not allow these
watchmen to work any more in the cargo holds. The Club also
request that the vacancies be filled by some unemployed
members - thus the regulations of the Union will be sustained.

Accordingly, we address you this letter with the
request that you will have these Watchmen replaced by members
of this Union - thus giving relief to some of the unemployed.

Yours faithfully,
Chinese Seamen's Union
Provisional Committee
Chang Yao Ming
Lu Hsiang Shi
Mar Chung Yien

“绥和”轮买办，

E-WO RIVER AND COAST STEAMERS TALLYMEN'S CLUB

Shanghai, August 15, 1935.

The Compradore,
S.S. "Suiwo"

Dear Sir,

We have received your letter contents of which
are noted. The matter has been referred to the Shanghai
Branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union for instructions.

With regard to your statement that you might
tell the watchmen to join the Union, this, we are afraid,
will not be agreeable to the Union. The reason is that
although some of the non-members of your steamers were allowed
to join the Union before, but that was during the time when
the Union were enlisting members. Now that registration had
been closed long ago and that unemployed members are so numerous,
there will be no possibility of altering our former decision.

Pending instructions from the Union, you are
requested to have the three watchmen suspended from working
in the cargo holds so that no misunderstanding will arise.
Otherwise, someone will have to bear the responsibility.

Trusting the matter will have your attention.

Yours faithfully,

Chan Yuen Loong
Executive Committee

怡和内河及沿海轮船理货员俱乐部

“绥和”轮买办，

先生台鉴：

关于阁下所述可能劝告看守员加入工会一事，恐怕工会不会同意。原因是，虽然此前贵轮的一些非会员曾被允许加入工会，但那是工会招募会员期间。现在注册早已关闭，且失业会员众多，不可能改变我们之前的决定。

在等待工会指示期间，请阁下暂停这三名看守员在货舱的工作，以免产生误解。否则，有人须承担责任。

相信阁下会关注此事。

此致
敬礼

陈元龙
执行委员会

Dear Sir,

S. I, Special Branch.
REPORT
No. D. 5293
Date. March 19, 1934.
Date 19 / 3 / 84
Subject (in full) Trouble among tea-boys on S.S. "Kungwo"
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by W. Duncan DFS

With reference to the attached report (Misc.74)
from Wayside Station giving an account of the trouble caused
on the evening of March 16 on the s.s. "Kungwo" by certain
disaffected tea-boys of that vessel, enquiries show that the
whole incident was the direct outcome of Messrs. Jardine,
Matheson & Co, Ltd's policy of offering to the travelling
public the benefits accruing from a Second or "B" Class fare.
In order to do this the Company had, of necessity, to rebuild
a certain section of the vessel which was formerly occupied
by Chinese passengers who were attended by the teaboys in
question under the comprador system.
These alterations necessitated a certain number of
tea-boys being discharged and according to the Company, it
was these men who boarded the ship and caused trouble.
That the local Chung Hwa Seamen's Union has been
more than interested in this incident is evidenced by the
fact that during the last few weeks, Sung Lih-ping (孫履平),
its secretary, has been most insistent that the Company employ
some of the deposed teaboys as Saloon-boys in the new "B"
Class accommodation of the s.s. "Kungwo". These boys being
of an extremely uncouth and untrained type to cater for the
needs of foreign and the better class of Chinese passengers,
Sung's proposal was flatly refused, with the result that
he adopted an attitude of being unable to guarantee that
there would not be any trouble on board the s.s. "Kungwo",
it being obvious from conversations he had held with the
Company, that he, on behalf of the Union, had guaranteed the
'discharged tea-boys immediate employment as Saloon boys
on the vessel in question.

日期 19 / 3 / 84
事由（全称）：“公和”轮（S.S. "Kungwo"）茶房伙计间的纠纷
制作人：D.S. Pitts 转呈人：W. Duncan DFS

关于附上的来自路边巡捕房（Wayside Station）的报告（杂项74），该报告叙述了3月16日晚在“公和”轮上由该船某些不满的茶房伙计引发的骚乱，经查询显示，整个事件直接源于怡和洋行有限公司（Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co, Ltd）向旅行公众提供二等或“B”等舱位票价优惠的政策。为了做到这一点，该公司不得不重建船上原先由买办制度下受上述茶房伙计侍候的中国乘客所占用的部分区域。
这些改建必然导致一定数量的茶房伙计被解雇，据该公司称，正是这些人登上船只并制造了麻烦。
中华海员公会对此事表现出极大的关注，其证据是，在过去几周内，该会秘书孙履平（Sung Lih-ping）一直极力坚持要求该公司雇佣部分被免职的茶房伙计，担任“公和”轮新设“B”等舱位的餐厅侍者（Saloon-boys）。由于这些伙计极其粗俗且未经训练，无法满足外国乘客及较高等级中国乘客的需求，孙的提议遭到断然拒绝，结果是他采取了一种无法保证“公和”轮上不会发生任何麻烦的态度。从他与该公司的谈话中可以明显看出，他代表公会已保证被解雇的茶房伙计能立即在该轮上获得餐厅侍者的工作。

Misc. 74.
Wayside
March, 16th, 34.

Trouble with tea boys on S.S. Kung Wo.

D.S. Fowler. D.I. Wardrop.

Sir,
At 8.55 p.m. 16.3.34 a telephone message was received from
the Chief officer of S.S. Kung Wo lying at the Old Ningpo Wharf
Kungping Road to the effect that trouble might arise from a number
of teaboys.
C.D.C. 241 and the under-signed attended and Mr. G.Blake.
Chief Officer of the Kung Wo of the Indo-China Steam Navigation
Coy Limited. 27 The Bund; was interviewed and the following facts
were ascertained.
The ship has just undergone a partial refit and alteration
in cabins etc. This was necessitated because a change from the
old system of 1st class, 2nd class and 3rd class Chinese on the
"B" Deck was contemplated. The result is, there is now no 1st and
2nd class Chinese cabins. They have been redesigned and fitted
as a foreign, but cheap rate fare, and consequently fewer cabins.
There are known as "B" class. The 3rd class remains as usual.
All the tea-boys who have apparently been engaged by the
Compradors (regardless of numbers) to work in the 2nd class, find
it is combined with the 1st class and fewer cabins and as a result
in-sufficient work for them.
All the tea boys are new to the ship; they having been
transferred from different boats of the Company for this boats first
trip since the refit.
At about 5 p.m. even date between 45 and 50 of the boys enter-
ed the "B" class saloon and stayed by the doors preventing stewards
and other persons from entering. Nothing further has since occurred
None of them advanced an explanation of this attitude.
（批：5/12 DS Note for enquiry C.Y. Podd 17/3）Mr. Clarke. Chief Officer states that he has communicated with
Mr. C.Y. Podd. General Manager, and that the companys' action at
present is passive. There are no passengers by the "B" class this
page_data.zh:
杂项 74.
路边巡捕房
1934年3月16日。

“公和”轮茶房伙计纠纷。

D.S. Fowler. D.I. Wardrop.

先生，
1934年3月16日晚上8点55分，接到停靠在公平路老宁波码头的“公和”轮大副的电话留言，称一些茶房伙计可能会引发麻烦。
中央巡捕房第241号警员及签署人前往现场，并会见了印度支那轮船公司有限公司（Indo-China Steam Navigation Coy Limited，地址：外滩27号）“公和”轮的大副 G.Blake 先生，查明了以下事实。
该船刚刚进行了部分翻新和客舱等处的改造。这是因为计划改变“B”层甲板原有的中国乘客一、二、三等舱制度。结果是，现在不再有一等和二等中国乘客客舱。它们已被重新设计并改装为面向外国人的廉价费率舱位，因此客舱数量减少。这些被称为“B”等舱。三等舱保持原样。
所有显然由买办雇佣（无论人数多少）在二等舱工作的茶房伙计发现，二等舱已与一等舱合并，且客舱减少，导致他们的工作量不足。
所有茶房伙计对该船来说都是新人；他们在该船翻新后的首次航行中从公司的不同船只调派而来。
当天下午5点左右，约45至50名伙计进入“B”等舱餐厅，守在门口，阻止服务员及其他人员进入。此后未发生其他事情。
他们均未对这种态度作出解释。
（批注：5/12 DS 备注供查询 C.Y. Podd 17/3）克拉克（Clarke）先生，即大副，表示他已与总经理 C.Y. Podd 先生取得联系，目前公司的行动是被动的。本次

will take the matter up with the British Consul.
The Ku gwo is due to sail at 4 a.m. 17.3.34 and should the
number of unnecessary tea-boys remain on the ship they will taken
along as a matter of course pending the Companys decision in the
matter.
(Boat not now sailing until 12 noon. 17/3/34)

page_data.en:
SMP HA
SHANGHAI, 17th March, 1934.
File No. 160.

Sir,

We beg to report that a number of teaboys invaded
the "B" Class Saloon on the S.S. "KUNGWO" whilst lying at Old
Ningpo Wharf last night and by their mere presence and numbers
prevented the steward staff from doing their work; with the re-
sult that we decided to close down and lock up the "B" Class
Saloon altogether rather than eject the teaboys and give them
the opportunity for which they were obviously looking of
creating a disturbance and possibly a serious incident.

We would explain that in keeping with the Company's
well-known policy, we decided to offer the travelling public
the benefit of a Second or "B" Class fare and in order to do
this, we had to rebuild a certain section of the ship which
was formerly occupied by Chinese passengers who were attended by
the teaboys in question under our compradore system. These al-
terations meant that a certain number of teaboys would be thrown
out of employment and it was these men who boarded our vessel
last night and interfered with the normal working of the vessel.
These teaboys were employed by our compradores and we were assured
that they had been adequately compensated by him for their loss
of employment and that there is no trouble at all in this regard.

For some two weeks past Mr. L.P. Sung of the Organisation
Committee of Chinese Seamen Union, Shanghai Branch (as per card
attached) has called on us and been most insistent that we employ
some of the deposed teaboys as Saloon boys in the new "B" Class
accommodation of the S.S. "KUNGWO" but we have steadfastly refused
to even consider this absurd proposal as the teaboys come of a
very low class, do not speak any English and are utterly untrained.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局总部
上海，1934年3月17日。
档案号 160.

先生，

谨此报告，昨晚停靠在老宁波码头时，一批茶房伙计闯入“公和”轮（S.S. "KUNGWO"）的“B”等舱餐厅，仅凭其存在和人数便阻碍了服务员员工开展工作；因此，我们决定完全关闭并锁上“B”等舱餐厅，而不是驱逐这些茶房伙计，从而给他们制造显然正在寻求的骚乱机会，甚至可能引发严重事件。

我们要说明的是，根据公司众所周知的政策，我们决定向旅行公众提供二等或“B”等舱位票价的优惠，为此，我们必须重建船上原先由买办制度下受上述茶房伙计侍候的中国乘客所占用的部分区域。这些改动意味着一定数量的茶房伙计将失业，而昨晚登上我们船只并干扰船只正常运作的正是这些人。
这些茶房伙计是由我们的买办雇佣的，我们得到保证，买办已就他们的失业给予了充分补偿，在这方面没有任何纠纷。

过去约两周以来，中华海员公会上海分会组织委员会的孙履平（L.P. Sung）先生（见附件名片）多次拜访我们，并极力坚持要求我们雇佣部分被免职的茶房伙计，担任“公和”轮新设“B”等舱位的餐厅侍者，但我们坚决拒绝甚至考虑这一荒谬提议，因为这些茶房伙计阶层极低，不懂英语，且完全未经训练。

page_data.en:
and unsuited for attending Foreign and the better class of
Chinese passengers who travel by our vessel in large numbers.
We did, however, suggest to Mr. Sung that we might
be willing to select two or three teaboys of good appearance
and address and train them as Saloon boys but this process
would be lengthy and a man would have to accept a nominal
pay for the period of training. Mr. Sung would not agree to
this and we were led to believe from his conversation that he
had guaranteed the teaboys employment in the Saloon of the
S.S. "KUNGWO" right away.
Under the circumstances, we felt that we had gone as
far as we could and we are obliged to let matters take their
course observing that Mr. Sung was at no pains to disguise the
threat that if we could not take on the teaboys as Saloon boys
immediately, he could not guarantee that there would not be
trouble on board the "KUNGWO".
The object of this letter is to request that you will
kindly protest on our behalf to the competent Chinese authorities
against the unwarranted intrusion and obstruction by the officials
of the Organization Committee of the Chinese Seamen's Union on
board the "KUNGWO" last night and to request that adequate steps
will be taken to prevent a repetition of the occurrence and for
which we must disclaim all responsibility.
We have the honour to be,
Sir,
Yours obedient servants,
JARDINE, MATHESON & Co., Ltd.
Sir John Brenan, K.C.M.G.,
H.B.M. Consul-General,

P.S. As we close this letter we learn that the No. 2 Steward of
the S.S. "KUNGWO" was badly beaten by teaboys last night and is at
present being attended by a doctor. This apparently is the only
serious incident of note which occurred last night and whilst we do
not attach very much importance, we feel obliged to request that you
will be good enough to protest against this assault as well.

且不适合侍候乘坐我们船只的大量外国乘客及较高等级的中国乘客。
然而，我们确实向孙先生建议，我们或许愿意挑选两三名仪表堂堂、举止得体的茶房伙计，并将他们培训为餐厅侍者，但这一过程将耗时较长，且在培训期间个人必须接受名义工资。孙先生不同意此方案，我们从他的谈话中得知，他已保证茶房伙计能立即在“公和”轮的餐厅获得工作。

本函旨在请求您代表我们向有关中国当局提出抗议，反对中华海员公会组织委员会官员昨晚在“公和”轮上的无理侵入和阻挠行为，并请求采取适当措施防止此类事件重演，对此我们必须声明不承担任何责任。

您顺从的仆人，
怡和洋行有限公司

Subject (in full) Indo-China Steam Navigation Company Tallymen

Made by P.S. Lingard Forwarded by Whouman ASS.

The situation up to date regarding the tallymen
employed on the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company's
ships is normal, all the men are at work and no dissatisfaction
among them is evident. The Chung Hwa Seamen's General
Labour Union, through its Secretary L.P. Sung, has expressed
dissatisfaction with the settlement that was made between
the compradores and tallymen, whereby the latter would
receive/$4 increase in their salary. The Union, evidently
with a view to bringing the tallymen under its control,
ordered the dissolution of the Tallymen's and Stevedores'
Union, and took up the matter of increase of salary for
the tallymen in order to gain their confidence. The Union
is insisting on payment of the $6 increase in salary
originally demanded by the tallymen. The China
Navigation Mutual Aid Association on behalf of the
compradores have offered to pay the Extra $2 to the
tallymen for a period of three months, but the Chung
Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union insists on payment of
the Extra $2 for a period of six months at least. So far
no compromise has been made.

These negotiations have all been made irrespective
of the feelings of the tallymen or their Union.

P.S. Lingard

Made by P.S. Lingard Forwarded by W Duncan DSS

A meeting was held on November 4 between Mr. L.P.
Sung (許達甫), Secretary of the Peace Preservation Corps
and the Organization Committee of Chung Hwa Seamen's General
Labour Union, and the management of the Indo China Steamship
Navigation Company, Ltd. when the situation of the unrest
among the tallymen of the latter firm was discussed.
Mr. Sung stated his reason for calling was to advise the
Management to force their Compradores to agree to the
Tallymen's demand for a further two dollars per month
increase in pay. The Compradores according to Mr. Sung
had only granted their Tallymen an increase of $4.00 per
month, whereas they had been instructed by the Company to
grant an increase of $6.00.
The Management replied that all their Tallymen
were quite content with the present state of affairs, and
that they had chopped a declaration last week to this
effect. Moreover the discontent alleged by Mr. Sung was
not in any way the fault of the Company, as the latter has in-
creased the Compradores' pay sufficiently to allow them to
increase all tallymens' wages by $6.00 a month - If Mr. Sung
had any complaints he could deal with the Compradores
who were the employers of the Tallymen.
The Compradores would be prepared, the Management
stated, to visit Mr. Sung personally between then and Tuesday,
November 7.
If by then they had not come to an agreement
with Mr. Sung, the Company would have all the chopped
declarations of the Tallymen, declaring their satisfaction
with their present pay, ready for Mr. Sung's perusal in their

Shanghai, 31st October, 1933.

Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.

Dear Sirs,

At the beginning of the present occasion, the Tallymen of your steamers, when asking for better treatment, had submitted three demands which were accepted on that day by your Manager, Mr. Tod. As we respected your promise, we issued instructions the next morning to all the Tallymen to resume work. The ships' Compradores, however, have declined, up to now, to observe these terms by signing an agreement accordingly on the plea that the increase given to them by the Company is not sufficient for them to carry out the terms. We then asked your Company about this and were told that the present increase you had given should enable the Compradores to have the terms carried out. As each party has made his own allegation, it raises some doubts concerning the sincerity of your Company in your acceptance of the terms and regarding the kind treatment to be accorded to labourers. Now the Tallymen of your various steamers are getting very indignant and the situation is so serious that it has passed the boiling point. Should the agreement be not signed within the shortest time, a big scale and effective demonstration may soon burst out. At that time, though it will be against our desire, we shall not be able to suppress the storm. We now like to know whether your Company could do anything towards this breach of promise by your Compradores as well as towards their obstruction. Now that the matter has come to a critical point, we write you again as a warning, and we also hope that you will give us an immediate reply; otherwise, we can but allow the Tallymen their freedom to take action.

Yours faithfully,
CHINESE SEAMEN UNION
Provisional Committee

上海，1933年10月31日。

致怡和洋行有限公司诸位先生：

在此次事件伊始，贵司轮船的理货员在请求改善待遇时，提出了三项要求，当日即获贵司经理 Tod 先生接受。鉴于我们尊重贵司的承诺，次日早晨我们便指令所有理货员复工。然而，贵司轮船买办至今拒绝签署相应协议以履行这些条款，借口是公司给予他们的加薪不足以让他们执行这些条款。随后我们就此询问贵司，被告知贵司目前给予的加薪应能使买办执行这些条款。由于各方各执一词，这令人对贵司接受条款的诚意以及对待劳工的友善态度产生疑虑。现在，贵司各轮船的理货员极为愤怒，局势如此严重，已达沸点。若不在最短时间内签署协议，大规模且有效的示威行动可能很快爆发。届时，尽管违背我们的意愿，我们将无法压制这场风暴。我们现在想了解，贵司能否就买办违背承诺及其阻挠行为采取任何措施。既然事态已到紧要关头，我们再次致函以示警告，并希望贵司立即回复；否则，我们只能允许理货员自由采取行动。

此致，
中华海员工会
临时委员会

TRANSLATION

Shanghai, 27th October, 1933.

Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.

Dear Sirs,

With regard to the 3 demands submitted by the Tallymen
of your steamers when asking for an increase of wages, we under-
stand from the letter received from your Manager Mr. Tod that you
had instructed the Compradores to have the matter settled for which
you feel thankful. But up to this moment, the Compradores have not
shown any sincerity of accepting these demands. As the incident
occurred last Saturday, one week has now elapsed, the Tallymen are
getting agitated. The situation is now serious and there is indica-
tion that there will be a second strike. In order to avert this
danger and to protect your business, we hope that you will instruct,
as soon as possible, your Compradores to sign the acceptance so
that the trouble will be settled. If this is not done, should any
thing be occurred, we cannot be held responsible. We hope you will
give us a reply before noon tomorrow.

Yours faithfully,
Yang Fu
Chang Chien Peh
Ling Ying
Executive Committee

Although the JARDINE MATHESON CO. LTD. has

Yesterday morning the BUREAU OF SOCIAL AFFAIRS

The PREPARATORY COMMITTEE OF THE CHINESE SEAMEN'S

At 10 a.m. yesterday at the request of the
compradores on various steamers, the BUREAU OF SOCIAL
AFFAIRS held a meeting of the representatives of both
parties. The CHINESE SEAMEN'S LABOUR UNION
did not agree to the meeting as the Central authorities
are taking over the responsibility of settling the demands
for an increase in the wages of the tallymen. Therefore

Furthermore the TALLYMEN'S CLUB was organized to deal
with the affairs of its members who are not formal members
of SEAMEN'S LABOUR UNION. So that no representatives from

meeting of some 10 compradores of various steamers was

The CHINESE SEAMEN'S LABOUR UNION at 3 p.m.

数名外籍及华籍高级职员在警方协助下，前往米勒路（Miller Road）、裕亨路（Yuheng Road）、梧州路（Wuchow Road）、西安路（Hsian Road）、汉璧礼路（Hanbury Road）等地的工人住所。他们将工人强行拉入汽车，送往工厂工作。约有30名工人被强迫复工。
“我们发布此消息以告公众，并再次声明，在纠纷得到满意解决之前，我们绝不复工。”

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

怡和洋行有限公司的劳工局势

虽然怡和洋行有限公司（JARDINE MATHESON CO. LTD.）已接受理货员提出的三项要求，但该公司买办拒绝签署协议。中国航业互助会（CHINA NAVIGATION MUTUAL ASSOCIATION）召集各轮船买办开会，商讨解决纠纷的措施，但未获结果。
昨日上午，社会局举行会议。
中华海员工会筹备委员会昨日召开紧急会议，讨论处理此事的措施。
昨日上午10时，应各轮船买办之请，社会局召开双方代表会议。中华海员工会不同意参加此次会议，因为中央当局正承担解决理货员加薪要求的责任。因此，无需其他当局进行调解。此外，理货员俱乐部（TALLYMEN'S CLUB）系为处理其成员事务而组织，这些成员并非海员工会的正式会员。因此，没有工人代表出席会议，也未通过任何决议。
10月29日，中国航业互助会收到中华海员工会的最后通牒信函，工会在信中表示，曾召集约10名各轮船买办开会，讨论给工人加薪3元一事（原要求为加薪6元）。
中华海员工会于昨日下午3时在其西门附近的会所召开紧急会议，讨论对付拖延纠纷的买办的措施。

At 4 p.m. October 27, two representatives of
the Ewo Tallymen named Tseng Zuan Jen (曾全仁) and Wong
Tseng-foh (王增富) called at the offices of the Shanghai
Branch of the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union,
33 Oong Ka Tsz Loong, City, and the Chinese Seamen's Special
Kuomintang, Chao Kia Road, City, and requested that the
compradores be urged to accept their demands. At both
places they were promised that their request would receive
attention, and that they should wait patiently until the
result is known of the negotiations now taking place.

The following are the demands which the
tallymen are pressing for through the medium of their
Union :-

1. That a flat increase of $6 per month in wages be granted
to all tallymen.

2. That any tallyman killed in the course of his duty be
given compensation equivalent to one year's wages which
is not to exceed $650, and that any one injured be given
compensation of $160 and re-employment on his recovery.

3. That the granting of annual bonus of one month's wages
to them at the end of each year be abolished and that
they be compensated every month by an increase in pay
equivalent to 3 days' wages.

It is learned that the compradores have now
agreed to accept these demands with the exception of No.1
which they have rejected, explaining that they can only
grant an increase of $3 in wages.

page_data.en:
FIVE SUGGESTIONS

1. If company wishes to make contract with compradores, the sum of the passage money must be considered by both sides with the moderate rate. That is, both sides settled it by the condition of the meantime market. If compradore side is not agree with the high rate what company declared, company can not change the compradore or get off his job by means of this subject.

2. A double pay must be paid by the compradores to all the staffs of their department at the end of the year. This is a traditional law for tens of years and also the Rule of the Union; hereafter such wages shall be paid by company, from compradore down to all his staffs.

3. Ships, unfortunately happened:- risk, damaged, drowned or old aged the ship must distincted or stopped to sail, company must pay all the prices of their furnitures, properties and the usual effects which made by compradores. Because every compradore has to pay the same to the former one, who continued from.

4. Risks happened by any ship, all the staffs and compradore himself, company must pay a certain amount for their lifes and properties, according to the International Sea Law(英國海商法) Except this, company shall apply the jobs or positions for compradores and staffs in the shortest time.

5. Company gives up a ship or any ship is not suitable for sailing, she must pay three months salaries or wages to the compradore and all his staffs, in case of lost job.
page_data.zh:
五项建议

1. 若公司希望与买办签订合同，船费金额必须由双方以合理费率予以考量。即，双方应根据当时的市场状况商定。若买办一方不同意公司所宣布的高费率，公司不得以此为由更换买办或解除其职务。

2. 买办必须在年底向其部门所有职员支付双薪。这是数十年的传统惯例，也是工会的规定；此后，此类工资应由公司支付，范围涵盖从买办至其所有职员。

3. 船只若不幸遭遇风险、损坏、沉没或因船龄老旧而必须区分停用或停止航行，公司必须支付由买办购置的所有家具、财产及日常用品的费用。因为每位买办都必须向其前任（即其继任的前任）支付同等费用。

4. 任何船只发生风险时，针对所有职员及买办本人的生命和财产，公司必须根据国际海商法（英國海商法）支付一定金额的赔偿。除此之外，公司应在最短时间内为买办及职员安排工作或职位。

5. 若公司放弃某艘船只或任何船只不再适航，公司必须向买办及其所有职员支付三个月的薪水或工资，作为失业补偿。

Sir,
At 8.30 p.m. 20/10/33, a telephone message was received at the
station from Mr. Jacobs, Hunts wharf, to the effect that the members
of Compradore's staff were being intimidated by the representatives
of the Seamen's Union.
Enquiries made by C.D.S.172 and the undersigned on the wharf
show that on 20/10/33 tallymen and stevedors of river boats were
granted an increase of pay. Then the tallymen and stevedors of
coast boats, walked out and went ashore, informing the compradors
that it was due to the fact that their pay was not increased.
At about 6 p.m. 31 tallymen of a river boat "Kung Wo" also left
their posts apparently with intent to support the movement of
coast-boat men. No untoward incidents occurred.
Three tallymen of S.S. "Kung Wo" remained on board and were
willing to carry on their work, but were afraid of interference on
the part of the Union. Wayside Station was notified and a guard
placed on the wharf. Altogether 69 men went on strike.

I am, Sir,

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... B. REGISTER File No. ...）

Subject (in full) Jardine & Matheson & Co., Ltd. - Employees'
Threatened Strike settled.

Made by F.P.S. Lingard Forwarded by [签名] C.W.T.

During an interview this afternoon,
Mr. Jacobs, Shipping Manager of the firm of Jardine
Matheson & Co., declared that the whole matter of
unrest among the tallymen of his Company had been
settled by mutual agreement.
He explained that the cause for the discontent
among the tallymen was as follows :-
Whereas on River steamers the above Company
employ their own tallymen, the coastal steamers'
tallymen are employed by Messrs. Jardine's compradores.
The basic pay for all tallymen was $6.00 per month per
man. During last May the firm of Jardine Matheson
gave all tally-men on river steamers an increase of
$3.00 a month, while the compradores on the coastal
steamers did not increase the pay of their tally-men.
Discontent set in and culminated in a depu-
tation from the coastal steamers tally-men calling on
the Manager of Messrs. Jardine Matheson & Co. on
Monday, October 16, to demand an increase of $3.00
per month per man in their pay, the same as had been
granted to the River steamer tally-men.
They stated that should the management not
agree to assure them of an increase by Friday,
October 20, they would declare a strike on that date.
This morning the management granted their
request, and in consequence all tally-men are working,
contentedly.

[左侧手写批注：Rh / M]

主题（全称）：怡和洋行有限公司（Jardine & Matheson & Co., Ltd.）—— 雇员威胁罢工事件已解决。

撰写人：F.P.S. Lingard 转呈人：[签名] C.W.T.

在今天下午的一次面谈中，
怡和洋行有限公司的航运经理雅各布斯先生（Mr. Jacobs）声明，该公司理货员之间的动荡局面已通过双方协议得到解决。
他解释说，理货员不满的原因如下：
鉴于上述公司在内河轮船上雇佣自己的理货员，而沿海轮船的理货员则由怡和洋行的买办雇佣。
所有理货员的基本工资为每人每月 6.00 元。去年五月，怡和洋行给予所有内河轮船理货员每月 3.00 元的加薪，而沿海轮船的买办并未增加其理货员的工资。
不满情绪由此产生，并最终导致沿海轮船理货员派出代表团，于 10 月 16 日（星期一）拜访怡和洋行有限公司经理，要求每人每月加薪 3.00 元，与内河轮船理货员所获加薪相同。
他们表示，如果管理层不保证在 10 月 20 日（星期五）之前同意加薪，他们将在该日宣布罢工。
今天上午，管理层同意了他们的请求，因此所有理货员都在安心工作。

Subject (in full) Unrest among Indo-China Steam Navigation Company
Compradores.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Duncan 1059

Unrest exists among compradores of the Indo-
China Steam Navigation Company (Jardine Matheson), who
are agitating for an increase in salary and emoluments
on the ground that they cannot meet their expenses
following the present decline in passenger traffic.
In addition they state that their employees (tallymen,
etc.) who were formerly content with their wages are
demanding an increase in pay. This latter demand
is a result of the recent tightening up of the work of
the Preventive Services of the Maritime Customs, whereby
the crews have had to abandon their hitherto lucrative
practice of smuggling.

In June, this year, the salaries of the
compradores (apart from commission) were raised from
$100 to $180 per mensem. The Company is now willing
to further increase the salaries to $300 per mensem
and pay in addition an extra ten per cent of the "Outside
broker" (compradore's agent) passenger business as well
as extra commission on tonnage carried by the steamer.
The compradores, however, are not satisfied with the
foregoing concessions and on June 25 representatives of the
Navigation Mutual Aid Society (compradores) submitted
the demands contained in the attached translation to the
company. The company has promised them a reply
within a few days. Developments will be made the
subject of a report in due course.

撰写人：D. S. Mac Adie 转呈人：W. Duncan 1059

印度支那轮船公司（怡和洋行）的买办中存在动荡局势，他们以目前客运量下降导致无法维持开支为由，煽动要求增加薪水和津贴。此外，他们还表示，其雇员（理货员等）以前对工资感到满意，现在也要求加薪。后一要求是由于海关缉私局近期加强工作所致，这使得船员们不得不放弃迄今有利可图的走私活动。

今年六月，买办的薪水（佣金除外）从每月 100 元提高到 180 元。公司现在愿意进一步将薪水提高到每月 300 元，并额外支付“外盘经纪人”（买办代理人）客运业务的百分之十，以及轮船承运吨位的额外佣金。然而，买办对上述让步并不满意，6 月 25 日，航海互助社（买办组织）的代表向公司提交了附译文中包含的要求。公司已承诺在几天内给予答复。事态发展将在适当时候另行报告。

---------
September .25, 1933.

The Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.,
Messrs. Jardine Matheson.

Sirs,

The Tallymen's Labour Union has
several times requested the compradores of
various steamers of your Company to increase
the pay of the tallymen and to improve their
treatment, and the whole body of compradores
have submitted five demands to 'your Company
for consideration. With a view to mediating
in the dispute, this Association has investigated
the facts in the dispute and has discovered
that your Company is in reality treating the
compradores in an exceedingly unfair manner so
much so that they are scarcely able to maintain
their present position. Being duty bound
to settle the dispute with the workers immediately
and to extricate the compradores from their
difficulties, the Association has decided to
submit five supplementary demands to your
management. As these demands as well as those
forwarded by the compradores are within reason,
it is hoped that your Company will accept them
so as to enable the employees on various steamers
to carry out their services peacefully and
faithfully and to improve the relationship
between the management and employees, which will
certainly be beneficial to the business of the
concern. This Association is sending Sung
Hwa-ding (沈華庭) and Chen Dah-chi (陳大器),
committee members of the Association, to you to
discuss basic measures for the improvement of
working conditions of the employees in question,
and hopes that your company will receive them and
discuss with them means for the settlement of
the dispute so as to cut short any possibility
of the dispute extending in scope.

Sung Hwa-ding (沈華庭)
Chang Yen-ling(?) (張延齡)
Van Zung-hwa (范宗華),
Members of the Standing Committee of
the Chung Hwa Navigation Cooperative
Association.

先生们，

理货员工会已多次请求贵公司各轮船买办增加理货员工资并改善其待遇，全体买办已向贵公司提交五项要求供考虑。为了调解纠纷，本协会调查了纠纷事实，发现贵公司实际上对待买办的方式极不公平，以至于他们几乎难以维持目前的地位。出于立即解决与工人的纠纷并使买办摆脱困境的责任，本协会决定向贵管理层提交五项补充要求。鉴于这些要求以及买办转达的要求均在合理范围内，希望贵公司予以接受，以便各轮船雇员能够和平、忠实地履行服务，并改善管理层与雇员之间的关系，这肯定有利于公司的业务。本协会派遣协会委员沈華庭（Sung Hwa-ding）和陈大器（Chen Dah-chi）前来与贵方讨论改善相关雇员工作条件的基本措施，并希望贵公司接见他们，并与他们讨论解决纠纷的方法，以缩短纠纷扩大的任何可能性。

沈華庭（Sung Hwa-ding）
张延龄(?)（Chang Yen-ling(?)）
范宗华（Van Zung-hwa），
中华航海合作协会常务委员会委员。

以下是五项补充要求：-

1. 若公司希望买办承包向乘客收取船票款项之事，承包金额应根据目前的业务状况确定。如果买办认为合同约定的金额过高且无法承担超额部分，公司不得因此解雇买办。

2. 按照惯例，买办会在十二月向职位低于买办的雇员发放双倍工资，以奖励其一年的良好服务。这笔额外支出应由公司补偿给买办，此外，公司还应向买办支付同一时期的双倍工资。

3. 当轮船失事、遭遇事故或因陈旧而无法使用时，公司应以现金赔偿买办的家具及私人物品。

4. 若船只遭遇不幸事故，幸存雇员应根据海事法获得公司赔偿，此外，公司应立即设法为他们安排就业。

5. 若轮船因无法使用而停运，公司应向职位低于买办的雇员发放相当于三个月工资的退休金（遣散费）。

On the afternoon of August 3, 1933, in connection
with the above mentioned letter, a visit was paid to Mr.
A. G. Jacobs, of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Co.,
No.27 The Bund. Mr. Jacobs stated that there had been
cases recently where the representatives of the "Tallymen
and Tea-boys Union" (Club) had boarded the vessels of the
Company in Shanghai for the purpose of soliciting members
but so far there had been no apparent disaffection among
the persons so approached nor any trouble during the
actual soliciting.

He pointed out that the present trouble with
the B. & S. Teaboys, which appeared likely to spread, was
that the Company had completely changed the system of
their employment, having taken the control of the teaboys
out of the hands of the compradores.

The following paragraphs serve to explain the
system under which the Chinese sea-borne passenger trade
is operated.

Shipping companies operating in the Chinese
Coast and River trade have for many years placed their
Chinese passenger trade in the hands of their respective
compradores, who in addition to obtaining the passengers
are looked upon to feed their charges during the journey.
This system has led to the employment by the compradores
of a No.1 Teaboy (or Chief Steward) who in turn employs
two, three or even four No.2 Teaboys (the number is usually
governed by the ship's size). The No.2 boys call to their
service several assistants who pay about $20.00 per round
trip for the privilege of working the ship (selling cakes,

由特别分部督察长 Golder 撰写，由警司 J W Robertson 转呈

1933年8月3日下午，就上述信函事宜，走访了位于外滩27号怡和轮船公司的 A. G. Jacobs 先生。Jacobs 先生表示，最近曾有“茶房与理货员公会”（俱乐部）的代表登上该公司在上海的船只招募会员，但截至目前，被接触人员中并未出现明显的不满情绪，在实际招募过程中也未发生任何麻烦。

他指出，目前宝顺洋行（B. & S.）茶房出现的、看似可能蔓延的麻烦，原因是公司完全改变了他们的雇佣制度，将茶房的控制权从买办手中收回。

以下段落旨在解释中国海上客运贸易的运作体系。

多年来，从事中国沿海及内河贸易的航运公司将其中国客运业务交由各自的买办负责，买办除了招揽乘客外，还负责在旅途中为乘客提供膳食。这一体系导致买办雇用了一名一号茶房（或称首席服务员），后者又雇用两、三甚至四名二号茶房（数量通常取决于船只大小）。二号茶房则雇用若干助手，这些助手需支付约20.00元的往返航程费用，以获得在船上工作（售卖蛋糕、

Periodically conditions on these river and

compradore's crew, which usually results in a dispute

It often happens that when tea-boys are evicted they

SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

With regard to our verbal request of the 29th ultimo,
that you would kindly investigate the report we had received that
representatives of a "Seamen's Union" had boarded our chartered
steamer, "Sandviken", and were endeavouring to enroll some members
of her crew, we have to report further that the same parties are
active again today on board our chartered steamer "Daviken" which
leaves for the South tomorrow morning.

We should like to take this opportunity of advising you
of the result of our own private investigations into the matter.
In the first place, we have found it difficult to obtain information
from our Chinese exactly who these men are that are trying to
interfere with our crews, which rather indicates that matters below
the surface are somewhat disturbing. It would seem that the
delegates who visit our ships come from the Tea-boys and Tallymen's
Union, who have an office in Seward Road (we attach for your
information their address in Chinese), and their object appears to
be twofold, namely :-

(1) To enroll as many Tea-boys and Tallymen in their
Union as they can, and

(2) To endeavour to persuade the Compradores of our
steamers to absorb some of the 200 Tea-boys
discharged from Messrs. B. & S's "Woosung".

So far as we have been able to gather, only one of our Compradores
has taken on some 10 to 15 ex-Teaboys of the "Woosung", and we are
advised that this was done under pressure from the Seamen's Union,
of Canton.

From the foregoing we judge that the actual sailors and
firemen of our vessels are not concerned in this affair, and that

(1) 尽可能多地招募茶房和理货员加入他们的工会，以及

the Tea-boys and Tallymen's Union, located in Seward Road, and
working in conjunction with the Seamen's Union of Canton seem
satisfied at the moment with endeavouring to enroll the Tea-boys and
Tallymen (almost synonymous terms) of our Coast and River ships in
their new Union with the object, presumably, of extending the very
serious labour dispute our friends, Messrs. B. & S., have with the
Seamen's Union of Canton.

The reason why our steamers' Compradores have been brought
into the picture is because the Tea-boys, who also act as Tallymen,
are engaged by them and not by us, and it would seem that the Tea-boys
and Tallymen cannot very well join the local Union without first having
obtained the sanction of, or come to some understanding with, their
employers, the ships' Compradores.

Our enquiries have thrown fresh light on this very serious
threat by the Canton Seamen's Union against Foreign Shipowners on the
China Coast and we are going into the matter with our Hong Kong
Principals, but in the meantime we consider that it would serve a
valuable purpose if it could be ascertained definitely, exactly what
relations the Tea-boys and Tallymen's Union of Seward Road have with
the Seamen's Union of Canton, and what the motives are behind the
enrolment of the Tea-boys on our Coast and River vessels in their Union.

In conclusion, we would add that we were rather hoping the
Tea-boy dispute on the Yangtsze steamers would be confined to the
but it would seem that the Seamen's Union of Canton, through the
Tea-boys and Tallymen's Union, are doing all they can to spread the
pel of discord on our Coast ships, through the medium of the dischar
Tea-boys from the C.N.Co's. "Woosung".

We should very much appreciate any assistance you may be
to give us, for we see in the activities of the Seamen's Union of Canto
and the local efforts of the Tea-boys and Tallymen's Union, all the
elements of a very serious commercial upheaval.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,
Per Pro. JARDINE, MATHESON & Co. LTD.

位于西华德路的茶房和理货员工会与广东海员工会合作，目前似乎满足于致力于将我们沿海和内河船舶上的茶房和理货员（几乎是同义词）招募到他们的新工会中，其目的大概是扩大我们的朋友B. & S.公司（即太古洋行）与广东海员工会之间非常严重的劳资纠纷。

我们轮船的买办被卷入其中，是因为兼任理货员的茶房是由他们雇佣而非由我们雇佣，而且茶房和理货员若不先获得雇主（即轮船买办）的许可或达成某种谅解，似乎很难加入本地工会。

我们的调查为广东海员工会对中国沿海外国船东发出的这一严重威胁提供了新的线索，我们正就此事项与我们的香港总行进行商讨，但与此同时，我们认为，如果能确切查明西华德路茶房和理货员工会与广东海员工会之间的关系，以及他们将我们沿海和内河船只上的茶房招募入会的动机，将具有宝贵的价值。

最后，我们要补充说，我们原本希望长江轮船上的茶房纠纷仅限于此，但看来广东海员工会正通过茶房和理货员工会，利用从中国轮船公司（C.N.Co.）“吴淞”号上解雇的茶房作为媒介，尽一切努力在我们的沿海船只上散布不和的种子。

如蒙提供任何协助，我们将不胜感激，因为我们在广东海员工会的活动以及茶房和理货员工会的本地努力中，看到了非常严重的商业动荡的所有要素。

此致，

Commissioner of Police,

The Seamen's Union must apply to the Settlement
authorities for permission to establish an office in the
Settlement. The Seamen's Union at No. 56 Sze Zeu Li
(四義里), East Seward Road, not being registered with the
Settlement authorities, has been holding meetings with

strike of tallymen of the s.s. "Loongwo" was the work
of the union. I hereby give the above information and
enclose herewith the address of the union for the purpose
of facilitating your inquiries for fear that its activities
may endanger the peace of the Settlement. I intended to
give my name but dare not do so for fear of publicity
because the members of this union are all radical elements.

In compliance with instructions from the Ewo Seamen's

increase of $5.00 per month to all tallymen, about 320 in
all. About 50 tallymen of the S.S. "Paowo" and "Luenho,"
of the same Company subsequently joined the strike.
Eventually, the Compradores of the vessels agreed to grant
a flat increase of $3.00 each per month with the result
that the strikers resumed at 3.30 p.m. the same day.

Yusang      (No.2 Buoy)
Loongwo     (Hunts Wharf)

Nantao and Chapei

The situation in the Mayar (Ching Wei) Factory
and the Mayar No.1 Silk Weaving Factory, both of which
are located on Shih Hwei Tung Road, Nantao, is practically
normal.

The 300 employees of the Mayar No.2 Silk Weaving
Factory, 619 Chaotung Road, Chapei, who struck on May 20,
1937, as a protest against the failure of the management
to observe the instructions of the Bureau of Social
Affairs regarding the grant of a 10% wage increase and
better treatment (Vide I.R. 21/5/37), returned to work
unconditionally this morning, July 3.

Indo-China Steam Navigation Company (British)
- Unrest among cabin boys

On June 24, the s.s. "Loongwu" left Shanghai for
Hankow, and on the following day, a notice was issued
to the effect that tips equivalent to 20% of the fare
would be collected from passengers for the cabin boys.
This decision met with opposition on the part of the 110
cabin boys, on the ground that they receive no wages from
the company but depend upon tips from passengers.
Consequently the cabin boys demanded that the order be
withdrawn, or in addition to the 20% tips they be granted
a monthly salary the same as that received by the cabin
boys of the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company. The
cabin boys have reported the matter through their delegate,
Zah Ah Tsing (石阿清) to the Shanghai Branch of the Chung
Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union, 680 Chung Hwa Road,
Nantao.

The S.S. "Loongwu" arrived here on July 2.
The Company has a total of eighteen vessels with
2,000 cabin boys. It is reported that all the cabin
boys will oppose the new order.

位于闸北曹东路619号的美亚第二丝织厂的300名员工曾于1937年5月20日罢工，抗议资方未遵守社会局关于给予10%加薪及改善待遇的指令（参见1937年5月21日情报报告），今晨（7月3日）已无条件复工。

印度支那轮船公司（英资）
- 舱侍中的不安情绪

6月24日，“龙武”号（s.s. "Loongwu"）离开上海前往汉口，次日发布通知，称将向乘客收取相当于票价20%的小费，供舱侍分配。这一决定遭到110名舱侍的反对，理由是他们在公司不领工资，全靠乘客小费为生。因此，舱侍们要求撤回该命令，或者在20%小费之外，给予他们与招商局轮船公司舱侍相同的月薪。舱侍们已通过其代表石阿清（Zah Ah Tsing）将此事项报告给位于南市中华路680号的中华海员总工会上海分会。

“龙武”号于7月2日抵达此处。
该公司共有十八艘船只，拥有2,000名舱侍。据报，所有舱侍都将反对这项新命令。

Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - Unrest among
tallymen of the s.s. "Prominent", Chinese name
"Kwangsang"

In connection with the opposition of twenty-one
tallymen of the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company's
s.s. "Prominent", to a decision of the new comprador of
the vessel to dispense with their services and to engage
new hands in their stead (Vide I.R. 3/2/37), a meeting
was held under the auspices of the Shanghai Branch of
the Hung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union, in the
office of the Ewo Tallymen's Guild, Lane 449, No.27

Seamen's Union to discharge those who are found to be
inefficient. He further promised to repatriate the
new hands who were engaged at Hongkong.

Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - unrest among tallymen
of the s.s. "Kwangsang"

Unrest now exists among the twenty-one tallymen of
the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company's s.s. "Kwangsang"
who are dissatissatisfied with a decision of the new comprador
of the vessel to dispense with their services and engage
new hands in their stead. These tallymen have referred
the matter to the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union,
Nantao. It is known that the Union authorities have
decided to request the management of the company to
instruct the comprador of the s.s. "Kwangsang" to cancel
his decision in order to avoid labour troubles.

The s.s. "Kwangsang" arrived at Hunts' Wharf from
Canton at 8 a.m. this morning, February 3.

management to sell the vessel in question to another
interest.

劳工 (6)

印度支那轮船公司 - “联和”轮理货员出现动荡

印度支那轮船公司所属“联和”轮（Luenho）的二十二名理货员目前出现动荡，他们正对管理层将该船出售给另一方的决定表示抗议。

这三名理货员代表前往位于市内的翁家宅路33号中华海员总工会，请求该组织提供协助。代表们要求，若管理层的决定付诸实施，应向他们发放相当于三个月工资的遣散费，并在出现空缺时优先录用他们。对方承诺将对此事进行调查，随后展开谈判。

（左侧手写批注：D. 5293）

April

Labour

Indo-China Steam Navigation Company - Unrest among
tallymen of s.s. "Tingsang" removed

Representatives of the "Ewo Steamship Tallymen's Club
(Lane 499, 43 Seward Road) and the "Preparatory Committee of
the Chung Hwa Seamen's General Labour Union (33 Oong Ka Ts
Loong, West Gate) called at the General office of Messrs
Jardine Matheson & Co., at 10 a.m. on April 20 and negotiated
with the comprador of the s.s. "Tingsang" (定生) for the
issue of a proportionate yearly bonus (known as the "double
pay for the last month of a year") equivalent to 26½ days'
pay for the period between January 1, 1933 and the day on
which it was determined to abolish this bonus system, i.e.
November 16, 1933 and 3 days' additional wages a month
which system was adopted commencing from November 16, 1933,
to replace the old double wage bonus system, to the tallymen
employed on the s.s. "Tingsang". Finally they were
promised that half of the yearly double wage bonus for 1933
would be issued to the tallymen of the s.s. "Tingsang" and
the 3 days' additional wage bonus system would be adopted
with effect from April 1.

New Engineering & Shipbuilding Works - Transient
stoppage of work - unrest

As a protest against the suspension of three of their
colleagues by the management, some 100 mechanics of the
New Engineering & Shipbuilding Works, a British concern
situated at No.640 Yangtszepoo Road, declared a "tai-kung"
strike at 4.30 p.m. April 20, but resumed work this
morning, April 21, pending mediation by the Bureau of Social
Affairs in connection with the dispute.
